requirements.text: The ESA sample(s) of the rear lamp submitted for type approval shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark and the type designation.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the submitted samples and confirm the trade name/mark and type designation are present, legible and survive a rub test.

requirements.text: ESA which are brought to the market as replacement parts do not need a type approval only if they are obviously marked as a replacement part by an identification number and if they are identical and from the same manufacturer as the corresponding original equipment.
requirements.test_case: Check that the replacement part carries an identification number and is identical to, and from the same manufacturer as, the original equipment.

requirements.text: In case the ESA is (part of) a light source, the applicant shall specify the approval number according to Regulation No. 37, Regulation No. 99 or Regulation No. 128 granted to this ESA, or provide a test report by a Technical Service designated by the Type Approval Authority stating that this ESA is not mechanically interchangeable with any light source according to Regulation No. 37, Regulation No. 99 or Regulation No. 128.
requirements.test_case: Verify the application includes either an R37/R99/R128 approval number or a Technical Service report confirming non-interchangeability.

requirements.text: The electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA) conforming to a type approved under this Regulation shall have an approval mark described in paragraph 5.3. affixed to it, except that no marking is required for electrical/electronic systems built into vehicles which are approved as units.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the production lamp and confirm the R10 approval mark per paragraph 5.3 is affixed.

requirements.text: The approval mark shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E", followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the mark and confirm a circle enclosing 'E' followed by the approving country's number.

requirements.text: The approval mark shall comprise the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number to the right of the circle specified in paragraph 5.3.1.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the mark and confirm '10R-' followed by the approval number is placed to the right of the circle.

requirements.text: The ESA(s) shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Review design and EMC test results confirming the lamp ESA meets R10 requirements in normal conditions of use.

requirements.text: The ESA(s) shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions, for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.
requirements.test_case: Confirm test reports exist covering radiated and conducted emissions and radiated and conducted immunity for the lamp ESA.

requirements.text: Before testing, a test plan shall be prepared in conjunction with the manufacturer, which contains at least mode of operation, stimulated function(s), monitored function(s), pass/fail criterion(criteria) and intended emissions.
requirements.test_case: Check that a test plan exists listing operating modes (position, stop, reversing), monitored functions, pass/fail criteria and intended emissions.

requirements.text: The electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.
requirements.test_case: Review the test report to confirm broadband radiated emission was measured per Annex 7 on a representative lamp sample.

requirements.text: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband limits shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz.
requirements.test_case: Measure broadband emission per Annex 7 from 30 to 75 MHz; all values must be below the logarithmically decreasing 62 to 52 dBµV/m limit.

requirements.text: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband limits shall be 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 6 to this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Measure broadband emission per Annex 7 from 75 to 400 MHz; all values must be below the 52 to 63 dBµV/m limit of Appendix 6.

requirements.text: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band the ESA broadband limit remains constant at 63 dB microvolts/m.
requirements.test_case: Measure broadband emission per Annex 7 from 400 to 1,000 MHz; all values must be below 63 dBµV/m.

requirements.text: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband limits shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz.
requirements.test_case: Measure narrowband emission per Annex 8 from 30 to 75 MHz; all values must be below the 52 to 42 dBµV/m limit.

requirements.text: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband limits shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 7.
requirements.test_case: Measure narrowband emission per Annex 8 from 75 to 400 MHz; all values must be below the 42 to 53 dBµV/m limit of Appendix 7.

requirements.text: The emission of ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
requirements.test_case: Perform ISO 7637-2 transient emission test per Annex 10 and record pulse amplitudes against Table 1.

requirements.text: For ESAs intended for vehicles with 12 V systems, the maximum allowed transient conducted emission pulse amplitude shall be +75 V for positive polarity and -100 V for negative polarity as given in Table 1.
requirements.test_case: Measure transient emission per ISO 7637-2; pass if positive pulses ≤ +75 V and negative pulses ≥ -100 V.

requirements.text: For ESAs intended for vehicles with 24 V systems, the maximum allowed transient conducted emission pulse amplitude shall be +150 V for positive polarity and -450 V for negative polarity as given in Table 1.
requirements.test_case: Measure transient emission per ISO 7637-2; pass if positive pulses ≤ +150 V and negative pulses ≥ -450 V.

requirements.text: The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.
requirements.test_case: Review test report to confirm radiated immunity testing per a method chosen from Annex 9.

requirements.text: The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) as described in Annex 9 with the test severity in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band given in Table 2a and the minimum test level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band given in Table 2b.
requirements.test_case: Verify the applied test levels in the Annex 9 test report match Table 2a and Table 2b for the chosen method.

requirements.text: For the BCI method, the ESA shall be tested at 60 mA in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 400 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 50 mA over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency band, as given in Tables 2a and 2b.
requirements.test_case: BCI test per Annex 9: confirm 60 mA over >90% and ≥50 mA over all of 20-400 MHz with no degradation.

requirements.text: For the ALSE method, the ESA shall be tested at 30 V/m in over 90 per cent and a minimum of 25 V/m over the whole 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency band, and at 10 V/m in over 90 per cent and a minimum of 8 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, as given in Tables 2a and 2b.
requirements.test_case: ALSE test per Annex 9: confirm 30/25 V/m (80-2000 MHz) and 10/8 V/m (2-6 GHz) levels applied with no degradation.

requirements.text: For the TEM cell method, the ESA shall be tested at 75 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 200 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 62,5 V/m over the whole 20 to 200 MHz frequency band, as given in Tables 2a and 2b.
requirements.test_case: TEM cell test per Annex 9: confirm 75 V/m over >90% and ≥62.5 V/m over all of 20-200 MHz with no degradation.

requirements.text: For the reverberation chamber method, the ESA shall be tested at 21 V/m in over 90 per cent and a minimum of 18 V/m over the whole LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency band, and at 7 V/m in over 90 per cent and a minimum of 6 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, as given in Tables 2a and 2b.
requirements.test_case: Reverberation chamber test per Annex 9: confirm 21/18 V/m (LUF-2000 MHz) and 7/6 V/m (2-6 GHz) with no degradation.

requirements.text: Where the ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, it shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.6.2. and with Annex 8.
requirements.test_case: Review schematic/BOM for oscillators >9 kHz; if none, narrowband compliance is deemed.

requirements.text: While tests are performed in accordance with Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall be considered as complying with immunity requirements if there is no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions".
requirements.test_case: Monitor lamp light output (stop/position/reversing) during Annex 9 exposure; pass if no degradation of immunity related functions.

requirements.text: The immunity of ESA representative of this type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 16750-2 for starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.
requirements.test_case: Confirm the test report covers starting profile and pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a, 3b per Annex 10 at Table 3a/3b levels.

requirements.text: For pulse 1, the ESA shall meet immunity test level -75 V (12V system) or -450 V (24V system) for 500 pulses with FPSC III for functions related to immunity and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity as specified in Table 3b.
requirements.test_case: Apply 500 pulses 1 at -75 V (12 V) / -450 V (24 V); pass if FPSC III achieved.

requirements.text: For pulse 3a, the ESA shall meet immunity test level -112 V (12V system) or -150 V (24V system) for 1 h with FPSC I for functions related to immunity and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity as specified in Table 3b.
requirements.test_case: Apply pulse 3a at -112 V (12 V) / -150 V (24 V) for 1 h; pass if FPSC I for immunity related functions and III otherwise.

requirements.text: The starting profile shall be tested according to the functional status classification as defined in ISO 16750-1.
requirements.test_case: Check the starting profile results are classified using ISO 16750-1 functional status classes.

requirements.text: The Functional Performance Status Classification (FPSC) as in ISO 7637-1 shall be applied for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b.
requirements.test_case: Check pulse test results are classified using ISO 7637-1 FPSC.

requirements.text: For the 12 V system starting profile (ISO 16750-2, test level II, 10 pulses), an ESA that shall be operational during engine start phases shall reach functional status class B if it performs immunity-related functions and class D if it does not, and any other ESA shall reach class C, as given in Table 3a; the starting profile applies only to ESAs that may be installed in vehicles with an internal combustion engine started by a 12 V / 24 V starter motor.
requirements.test_case: Apply ISO 16750-2 starting profile level II, 10 pulses; verify required functional status class (B/C/D) is met.

requirements.text: ESAs with no immunity related functions need not be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.8. and with Annex 9 to this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Review function analysis; if no immunity related functions, radiated immunity compliance is deemed.

requirements.text: ESAs that are not switched, contain no switches or do not include inductive load need not be tested for transient conducted emission and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.
requirements.test_case: Review circuit design for switches/inductive loads; if absent, transient emission compliance is deemed.

requirements.text: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband limits shall be 62 to 52 dBµV/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, and 52 to 63 dBµV/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 6; in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band the limit remains constant at 63 dBµV/m.
requirements.test_case: Measure broadband radiated emissions per Annex 7 from 30 to 1,000 MHz and verify all values are below the 62-52 / 52-63 / 63 dBµV/m limit line.

requirements.text: On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband values, expressed in dBµV/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
requirements.test_case: Compare measured broadband emission values in dBµV/m against the paragraph 7.10.2.1 limits; pass if all are below.

requirements.text: In the frequency range 30-75 MHz, the broadband radiated emissions of the electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA) shall not exceed the reference limit E = 62 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m at frequency F (MHz), measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth (see paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1.).
requirements.test_case: Measure ESA broadband radiated emissions at 30-75 MHz with 120 kHz bandwidth per Annex 7; pass if all values are below 62 - 25.13 log(F/30) dBµV/m.

requirements.text: In the frequency range 75-400 MHz, the broadband radiated emissions of the electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA) shall not exceed the reference limit E = 52 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m at frequency F (MHz), measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth (see paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1.).
requirements.test_case: Measure ESA broadband radiated emissions at 75-400 MHz with 120 kHz bandwidth per Annex 7; pass if all values are below 52 + 15.13 log(F/75) dBµV/m.

requirements.text: In the frequency range 30-75 MHz, the narrowband radiated emissions of the electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA) shall not exceed the reference limit E = 52 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m at frequency F (MHz), measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth (see paragraph 6.6.2.1.).
requirements.test_case: Measure ESA narrowband radiated emissions at 30-75 MHz with 120 kHz bandwidth per Annex 8; pass if all values are below 52 - 25.13 log(F/30) dBµV/m.

requirements.text: For an ESA powered by LV, a 5 µH / 50 Ω artificial network (AN) as defined in Figure 1 shall be used during testing.
requirements.test_case: Review the test setup/report to confirm a 5 µH / 50 Ω AN per Figure 1 was used on the LV supply lines.

requirements.text: For an ESA powered by LV, the AN(s) shall be mounted directly on the ground plane and the grounding connection of the AN(s) shall be bonded to the ground plane.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the test setup to confirm the AN is mounted directly on and bonded to the ground plane.

requirements.text: For an ESA powered by LV, the measurement ports of the AN(s) shall be terminated with a 50 Ω load.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the test setup to confirm AN measurement ports are terminated with 50 Ω loads.

requirements.text: If not otherwise stated in Annex 7, the test measuring broadband electromagnetic emissions from the ESA shall be performed according to CISPR 25.
requirements.test_case: Review the test report and confirm the radiated broadband emission test followed CISPR 25 unless Annex 7 states otherwise.

requirements.text: During the radiated broadband emission test, the ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
requirements.test_case: Check the test set-up record shows all lamp functions (position, stop, reversing) operating normally, at maximum load where possible.

requirements.text: For ESA other than involved in "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the radiated broadband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25.
requirements.test_case: Verify in the test report that the ALSE method of CISPR 25 Clause 6.4 was used (or an OATS per CISPR 16-1-4 as permitted alternative).

requirements.text: To ensure there is no extraneous noise or signal sufficient to affect materially the measurement, ambient measurements shall be taken before or after the main test, and the extraneous noise or signal shall be at least 6 dB below the limits of interference given in paragraph 6.5.2.1., except for intentional narrowband ambient transmissions.
requirements.test_case: Check the ambient scan recorded before or after the main test is at least 6 dB below the paragraph 6.5.2.1. limits.

requirements.text: The radiated broadband emission limits apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS.
requirements.test_case: Confirm emissions measured over 30 to 1,000 MHz remain below the paragraph 6.5. broadband limits.

requirements.text: If peak detectors are used for the radiated broadband emission measurements, a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied.
requirements.test_case: Review the report: where peak detection is used, verify a 20 dB correction was applied before comparing with the quasi-peak limits.

requirements.text: The radiated broadband emission measurements shall be performed with a spectrum analyser or a scanning receiver using the parameters defined in Table 1 and Table 2.
requirements.test_case: Check instrument settings (RBW 120 kHz, scan/dwell times, step size) in the report match Table 1 or Table 2.

requirements.text: Unless otherwise specified, the configuration with the LV harness closer to the antenna shall be tested, and the phase centre of the antenna shall be in line with the centre of the longitudinal part of the wiring harnesses for frequencies up to 1,000 MHz.
requirements.test_case: Inspect test set-up photos to confirm harness orientation and antenna phase centre alignment with the harness centre.

requirements.text: In the event that the limit is exceeded during the radiated broadband emission test, investigations shall be made to ensure that this is due to the ESA and not to background radiation.
requirements.test_case: Where any exceedance is recorded, verify the report documents an investigation distinguishing ESA emission from background.

requirements.text: The maximum of the readings relative to the limit (horizontal/vertical polarization) in each of the 14 frequency bands shall be taken as the characteristic reading at the frequency at which the measurements were made.
requirements.test_case: Check the report evaluates the maximum reading of both polarizations per frequency band against the limit.

requirements.text: The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load, during the narrowband emission tests.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the test plan and report show the lamp operated in normal mode with all functions (position, stop, reversing) energised at maximum load.

requirements.text: The narrowband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in paragraph 6.4. of CISPR 25.
requirements.test_case: Check the test report confirms the ALSE set-up per CISPR 25 paragraph 6.4 (or an OATS complying with CISPR 16-1-4 as alternative).

requirements.text: Ambient measurements shall be taken before or after the main test, and the extraneous noise or signal shall be at least 6 dB below the limits of interference given in paragraph 6.6.2.1. of this Regulation, except for intentional narrowband ambient transmissions.
requirements.test_case: Review the ambient scan in the test report and confirm the ambient is at least 6 dB below the paragraph 6.6.2.1 limits.

requirements.text: The narrowband emission limits apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).
requirements.test_case: Measure radiated narrowband emissions from 30 to 1,000 MHz and confirm all readings are below the paragraph 6.6.2.1 limits.

requirements.text: The narrowband emission measurements shall be performed with an average detector.
requirements.test_case: Check the receiver settings in the test report specify an average detector.

requirements.text: The narrowband emission measurements shall be performed with a spectrum analyser or a scanning receiver using the parameters defined in Tables 1 and 2 (spectrum analyser: RBW 100/120 kHz at -3 dB, minimum scan time 100 ms/MHz; scanning receiver: BW 120 kHz at -6 dB, maximum step size 60 kHz, minimum dwell time 5 ms, for 30 to 1,000 MHz).
requirements.test_case: Verify the instrument settings in the test report match Table 1 or Table 2 parameters.

requirements.text: In the event that the narrowband limit is exceeded during the test, investigations shall be made to ensure that this is due to the ESA and not to background radiation including broadband radiation from the ESA.
requirements.test_case: For any exceedance, confirm the report documents an investigation distinguishing ESA narrowband emission from background or broadband radiation.

requirements.text: The ESA may comply with the requirements of any combination of the test methods (absorber chamber ISO 11452-2, TEM cell ISO 11452-3, bulk current injection ISO 11452-4, stripline ISO 11452-5, reverberation chamber ISO 11452-11) at the manufacturer's discretion, provided that these result in the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of this Annex being covered.
requirements.test_case: Review the immunity test plan/report and confirm the chosen methods together cover the full 20 to 6,000 MHz range.

requirements.text: For the immunity test of the ESA, the frequency range and general test conditions shall be based on ISO 11452-1.
requirements.test_case: Check the test report states frequency range and general test conditions per ISO 11452-1.

requirements.text: The test conditions for the ESA immunity test shall be according to ISO 11452-1.
requirements.test_case: Verify in the test report that test conditions comply with ISO 11452-1.

requirements.text: The ESA under test shall be switched on and shall be stimulated to be in normal operation condition.
requirements.test_case: Confirm during test that lamp functions (position, stop, reversing) are powered and operating normally.

requirements.text: The ESA under test shall be arranged as defined in this Annex unless individual test methods dictate otherwise.
requirements.test_case: Inspect test setup photos/report for arrangement per Annex 9 or the applicable ISO 11452 part.

requirements.text: Any extraneous equipment required to operate the ESA under test shall not be in place during the calibration phase, and no extraneous equipment shall be closer than 1 m from the reference point during calibration.
requirements.test_case: Check calibration records show no extraneous equipment present and none within 1 m of the reference point.

requirements.text: The test signal generating equipment and its layout shall be to the same specification as that used during each appropriate calibration phase.
requirements.test_case: Compare test and calibration setup records for identical signal generating equipment and layout.

requirements.text: If the ESA under test consists of more than one unit and the vehicle wiring harnesses are not available, the length between the electronic control unit and the AN shall be as defined in the standard.
requirements.test_case: Measure the harness length between ECU and AN in the setup and compare with the ISO 11452 value.

requirements.text: Immunity measurements of the ESA shall be made in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range with frequency steps according to ISO 11452-1.
requirements.test_case: Verify the test report covers 20 to 6,000 MHz with ISO 11452-1 frequency steps.

requirements.text: In the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, the test signal modulation shall be AM (amplitude modulation), with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Check generator settings in report: AM 1 kHz, 80 % depth for 20-400 MHz.

requirements.text: In the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, the test signal modulation shall be PM2 (pulse modulation type 2), Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Check generator settings in report: PM2 Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs for 2,700-3,100 MHz.

requirements.text: In the 380 to 2,700 MHz and the 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, the test signal modulation shall be PM3 (pulse modulation type 3), Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Check generator settings in report: PM3 Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs for 380-2,700 and 3,100-6,000 MHz.

requirements.text: The frequency step size and dwell time shall be chosen according to ISO 11452-1.
requirements.test_case: Verify step size and dwell time in the report comply with ISO 11452-1.

requirements.text: The test shall be performed at the intervals specified in ISO 11452-1, throughout the frequency range 20 to 6,000 MHz.
requirements.test_case: Check the report shows test points at ISO 11452-1 intervals over 20-6,000 MHz (or accredited data with spot frequencies).

requirements.text: If the ESA fails the tests defined in this Annex, it shall be verified as having failed under the relevant test conditions and not as a result of the generation of uncontrolled fields.
requirements.test_case: For any failure, review field monitoring data to confirm failure occurred under controlled test conditions.

requirements.text: For the absorber chamber test, the "substitution method" shall be used to establish the test field conditions according to ISO 11452-2.
requirements.test_case: Verify the report states substitution method field calibration per ISO 11452-2.

requirements.text: For the absorber chamber test, the test shall be performed with vertical polarization.
requirements.test_case: Check antenna polarization recorded in the report is vertical.

requirements.text: For TEM cell testing, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-3.
requirements.test_case: Verify the TEM cell test report references and follows ISO 11452-3.

requirements.text: For bulk current injection testing, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-4 on a test bench with either the BCI substitution method and injection probe positioned at 150 mm distance to the ESA, or the BCI closed loop method and injection probe positioned at 900 mm distance to the ESA.
requirements.test_case: Check report for ISO 11452-4 bench test with probe at 150 mm (substitution) or 900 mm (closed loop).

requirements.text: For the reverberation chamber test, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-11 and, unless otherwise specified, using a test setup with ground plane.
requirements.test_case: Verify the report follows ISO 11452-11 with a ground plane setup.

requirements.text: The test method for the ESA shall ensure the immunity of ESAs to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply and limit conducted transients from ESAs to the vehicle power supply.
requirements.test_case: Review the conducted transient test plan and report to confirm both immunity and emission transient tests on the power supply are covered.

requirements.text: For immunity against transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines, the test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to the International Standard ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the supply lines as well as to other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
requirements.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b to the lamp supply and related lines and verify the functional performance status meets the required class.

requirements.text: For immunity against transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines, the starting profile according to the International Standard ISO 16750-2 shall be applied to the supply lines as well as to other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines; ESAs that are exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles (vehicles without 12V/24V starter motor) are not subject to starting profile.
requirements.test_case: Apply the ISO 16750-2 starting profile to the lamp supply lines and verify the functional status classification is met, or document EV-only exclusivity.

requirements.text: The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by ESAs on 12/24 V supply lines shall be measured according to the International Standard ISO 7637-2 on supply lines as well as to other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
requirements.test_case: Measure conducted transient emissions from the lamp per ISO 7637-2 on supply lines and verify they are within the regulation limits.

requirements.text: The external surface of the vehicle (including the rear lamp lens and housing) shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any pointed or sharp parts or any projections of such shape, dimensions, direction or hardness as to be likely to increase the risk or seriousness of bodily injury to a person hit by the external surface or brushing against it in the event of a collision.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the installed rear lamp's outer surface for outward-directed pointed or sharp parts or injurious projections; pass if none are found.

requirements.text: The external surface of the vehicle (including the rear lamp lens and housing) shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any part likely to catch on pedestrians, cyclists or motor cyclists.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the installed rear lamp for outward-directed hooks, edges or features likely to catch; pass if none are found.

requirements.text: No protruding part of the external surface (including the rear lamp lens and housing) shall have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm.
requirements.test_case: Measure the radii of curvature of the protruding parts of the installed rear lamp with radius gauges; pass if all are at least 2.5 mm.

requirements.text: The radius of curvature requirement shall not apply to parts of the external surface which protrude less than 5 mm, but the outward facing angles of such parts shall be blunted, save where such parts protrude less than 1.5 mm.
requirements.test_case: Measure the protrusion of the rear lamp parts; for parts protruding between 1.5 mm and 5 mm, verify that their outward-facing angles are blunted.

requirements.text: For protruding parts of the external surface made of a material of hardness not exceeding 60 Shore A having a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm, the hardness measurement shall be taken with the component as installed on the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Measure the Shore A hardness of the soft protruding parts with the lamp installed on the vehicle; pass if hardness is at most 60 Shore A.

requirements.text: Where it is impossible to carry out a hardness measurement by the Shore A procedure, comparable measurements shall be used for evaluation.
requirements.test_case: Verify that an equivalent hardness measurement method was used and documented where the Shore A procedure is not feasible.

requirements.text: The dimension of the projection of the rear lamp mounted on a convex surface may be determined either directly or by reference to a drawing of an appropriate section of this component in its installed condition.
requirements.test_case: Measure the installed lamp's projection directly or from an installed-condition section drawing, and check it against the applicable limit.

requirements.text: If the dimension of the projection of the rear lamp mounted on a surface other than convex cannot be determined by simple measurement, it shall be determined by the maximum variation of the distance of the centre of a 100 mm diameter sphere from the nominal line of the panel when the sphere is moved over and is in constant contact with that component.
requirements.test_case: Move a 100 mm diameter sphere over the installed lamp in constant contact and record the maximum variation of the sphere centre from the nominal panel line; use this as the projection dimension and check it against the applicable limit.

requirements.text: The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which they may be subjected, they retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation and enable the vehicle to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp mounting on the vehicle and check after vibration in normal use that the lamp keeps its prescribed position, orientation and characteristics.

requirements.text: It shall not be possible for the lamps to be inadvertently maladjusted.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the fixing and adjustment means to confirm the lamp cannot be maladjusted without deliberate action.

requirements.text: For all light-signalling devices, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3° in each direction.
requirements.test_case: Measure the installed reference axis of each rear function relative to the road plane; pass if within ±3°.

requirements.text: For the rear signalling devices (other than side retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps), the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3° in each direction.
requirements.test_case: Measure the installed reference axis relative to the vehicle median longitudinal plane; pass if parallel within ±3°.

requirements.text: Any specific instructions as regards fitting laid down by the manufacturer shall be complied with.
requirements.test_case: Compare the installation against the manufacturer's fitting instructions; pass if all instructions are followed.

requirements.text: In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the lamps shall be verified with the vehicle unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the condition defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2.
requirements.test_case: Place the unladen vehicle on a flat horizontal surface and measure the lamp height and orientation.

requirements.text: In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall be fitted to the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane (this estimate to be based on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp and not on the edge of its illuminating surface referred to in paragraph 2.10.3.).
requirements.test_case: Measure the left and right lamp positions from the median longitudinal plane; pass if symmetrical based on the exterior lamp form.

requirements.text: In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane; this requirement is not valid with regard to the interior structure of the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Compare the exterior geometry of the left and right lamps; pass if they are mirror-symmetrical.

requirements.text: In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity of the left and right lamps of each function; pass if both meet the same colour requirements.

requirements.text: In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics; this shall not apply to a matched pair of a function.
requirements.test_case: Compare the photometric test results of the left and right lamps; pass if substantially identical.

requirements.text: In case of lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo, only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo can be fitted on the rear of the vehicle, and all logos that are not vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer logos are prohibited.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the rear lamps for logos; pass if there is at most one logo per side or one central logo and only vehicle or body manufacturer logos are used.

requirements.text: On vehicles whose external shape is asymmetrical, the requirements for lamps constituting a pair shall be satisfied so far as is possible.
requirements.test_case: Assess the pair symmetry on the asymmetrical vehicle; pass if the pair requirements are met as far as possible.

requirements.text: Lamps grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with one another shall fulfil all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and other requirements, if any.
requirements.test_case: Verify each function in the combination lamp separately for colour, position, orientation, visibility and wiring; pass if all requirements are met.

requirements.text: The photometric and colorimetric requirements of a lamp shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which this lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF.
requirements.test_case: Measure each function (position, stop, reversing) with the other functions switched OFF; pass if its photometric and colour limits are met.

requirements.text: When a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other function(s) which can be switched ON together with it, the requirements regarding colour of each of these other functions shall be fulfilled when the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the rear position lamps are switched ON.
requirements.test_case: Switch ON the rear position lamp together with the reciprocally incorporated function and measure chromaticity; pass if within the colour limits.

requirements.text: Stop lamps and direction-indicator lamps are not permitted to be reciprocally incorporated.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the design to confirm the stop lamp and any direction indicator do not share a light source or light-emitting surface.

requirements.text: Where stop lamps and direction-indicator lamps are grouped, any horizontal or vertical straight line passing through the projections of the apparent surfaces of these functions on a plane perpendicular to the reference axis shall not intersect more than two borderlines separating adjacent areas of different colour.
requirements.test_case: Project the apparent surfaces and draw horizontal and vertical lines; pass if no line crosses more than two colour borderlines.

requirements.text: Where stop lamps and direction-indicator lamps are grouped, their apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis, based upon the areas bounded by the outline of their light emitting surfaces, shall not overlap.
requirements.test_case: Project the apparent surfaces along the reference axis; pass if the stop and direction-indicator surfaces do not overlap.

requirements.text: Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.14.11.1., subparagraph (a), the apparent surface of which is composed of two or more distinct parts, shall be installed in such a way that either the total area of the projection of the distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projection of the said apparent surface, or the minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the apparent surface does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis; these requirements shall not apply to a single retro-reflector.
requirements.test_case: Measure the projected apparent surface parts; pass if they fill at least 60 % of the circumscribing quadrilateral or the gap between facing edges is at most 75 mm.

requirements.text: Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1., subparagraph (b) or (c), composed of two lamps marked "D" or two independent retro reflectors, shall be installed in such a way that either the projection of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of the two lamps or retro reflectors occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing these projections, or the minimum distance between the facing edges of the apparent surfaces does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.
requirements.test_case: Measure the projected apparent surfaces of the two units; pass if they fill at least 60 % of the circumscribing quadrilateral or the edge gap is at most 75 mm.

requirements.text: Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1., subparagraph (d) shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.
requirements.test_case: Apply the 60 % or 75 mm criteria of paragraph 5.7.2.1. to the interdependent lamp system; pass if one is met.

requirements.text: Two lamps or an even number of lamps in the shape of a band or strip shall be placed symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, extending on both sides to within at least 0.4 m of the extreme outer edge of the vehicle, and shall be not less than 0.8 m long; the illumination of such a surface shall be provided by not less than two light sources placed as close as possible to the ends.
requirements.test_case: Measure the strip length, symmetry, distance to the vehicle outer edge and light source positions; pass if they meet the stated limits.

requirements.text: Red light emitted by a lamp fitted on the rear of the vehicle (as defined in paragraph 2.1.5.) shall not be visible from the front of the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the installed lamp from the front of the vehicle; no red light from the rear lamp shall be visible.

requirements.text: The maximum height above the ground shall be measured from the highest point and the minimum height from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.
requirements.test_case: Measure the highest and lowest points of each function's apparent surface above the ground; check them against the height limits.

requirements.text: For the purposes of reducing the geometric visibility angles, the position of a lamp with regard to height above the ground shall be measured from the H plane.
requirements.test_case: Measure the lamp height from the H plane when applying reduced vertical visibility angles.

requirements.text: The position of the rear lamps, as regards width, shall be determined from that edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is the furthest from the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle when referred to the overall width, and from the inner edges of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis when referred to the distance between lamps.
requirements.test_case: Measure lateral position from the outer and inner edges of the apparent surface in the reference axis direction and check that the values used for compliance follow this method.

requirements.text: In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) of the rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.
requirements.test_case: Operate each function and observe/measure intensity, colour and apparent surface over time; no intentional variation is permitted.

requirements.text: Any variation of the photometric characteristics of the lamp in relation to the ambient light, as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, or when the lamp is being used to provide another lighting function, shall be in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.
requirements.test_case: Measure photometry in each varying operating state and verify compliance with the lamp's device approval provisions.

requirements.text: For the visibility of red light towards the front of a vehicle, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a red lamp if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (see Annex 4).
requirements.test_case: Observe from Zone 1 in a transverse plane 25 m in front of the vehicle per Annex 4; the red apparent surfaces shall not be directly visible.

requirements.text: In case of doubt, the requirement on visibility of red light to the front shall be deemed fulfilled if the luminous intensity of the red light emitted to the front, as verified during type approval of the lamps, is not more than 0.25 cd per lamp taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensity of red light emitted towards the front, including body influence; pass if ≤ 0.25 cd per lamp.

requirements.text: The electrical connections shall be such that the rear position lamps, the front position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps, if they exist, the side-marker lamps, if they exist, and the rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
requirements.test_case: Operate the vehicle lighting switch and verify the rear position lamps switch ON and OFF simultaneously with the other listed lamps (except in the 5.11.1 conditions).

requirements.text: In the case of an interdependent lamp system, all light sources shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
requirements.test_case: Switch the function ON and OFF and verify all light sources of the interdependent system change state simultaneously.

requirements.text: The concealment of the rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors shall be prohibited.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the installation; the rear lamp shall not be fitted with any concealment device.

requirements.text: The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
requirements.test_case: Measure chromaticity of the reversing lamp and verify it is within the white boundaries.

requirements.text: The colour of the light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
requirements.test_case: Measure chromaticity of the stop lamp and verify it is within the red boundaries.

requirements.text: The colour of the light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
requirements.test_case: Measure chromaticity of the rear position lamp and verify it is within the red boundaries.

requirements.text: The colour of the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be red.
requirements.test_case: Measure the colour of the retro-reflected light and verify it is red.

requirements.text: The number of rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Count installed lamps per function and compare with the individual specifications in paragraph 6.

requirements.text: The lamp may be installed on movable components only provided that the conditions specified in paragraphs 5.18., 5.19. and 5.20. are fulfilled.
requirements.test_case: Verify, for a lamp on a movable component, that 5.18, 5.19 and 5.20 are met.

requirements.text: Rear position lamps and rear retro-reflectors may be installed on movable components only if at all fixed positions of the movable components the lamps on the movable components meet all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for those lamps.
requirements.test_case: Place the movable component in each fixed position and verify position, geometric visibility, colour and photometry of the lamps.

requirements.text: Where the rear position lamp or rear retro-reflector functions are obtained by an assembly of two lamps marked "D", only one of the lamps needs to meet the position, geometric visibility and photometric requirements for those lamps at all fixed positions of the movable components.
requirements.test_case: At all fixed positions of the movable component, verify at least one of the "D" lamps meets position, geometric visibility and photometric requirements.

requirements.text: Where additional lamps for the rear position lamp or rear retro-reflector functions are fitted and are switched ON when the movable component is in any fixed open position, these additional lamps shall satisfy all the position, geometric visibility and photometric requirements applicable to the lamps installed on the movable component.
requirements.test_case: With the movable component in each fixed open position, verify the additional lamps meet position, geometric visibility and photometric requirements.

requirements.text: Where the rear position lamp function is obtained by an interdependent lamp system completely mounted on the moving component(s), the requirements of paragraph 5.18.1. shall be satisfied, and any additional lamps switched ON when the movable component is in any fixed open position shall satisfy all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements applicable to the lamps installed on the movable component.
requirements.test_case: Verify 5.18.1 compliance at all fixed positions and compliance of any additional lamps.

requirements.text: Where the rear position lamp function is obtained by an interdependent lamp system partly mounted on the fixed component and partly mounted on a movable component, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the Applicant during the device approval procedure shall meet all the position, outwards geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for those lamps, at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).
requirements.test_case: At all fixed positions of the movable component, verify the specified interdependent lamp(s) meet position, outward visibility, colour and photometry, and inward photometric values.

requirements.text: When the movable components are in a position other than a "normal position of use", the devices installed on them shall not cause undue discomfort to road users.
requirements.test_case: Assess the lamp with the movable component open; no undue discomfort (e.g. glare) to road users.

requirements.text: When the lamp is installed on a movable component and the movable component is in the "normal position(s) of use", the lamp shall always return to the position(s) specified by the manufacturer in accordance with this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Cycle the movable component and verify the lamp returns to the manufacturer-specified position.

requirements.text: The apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of rear position lamps and retro-reflectors shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component, with or without a light-signalling device installed on it, in any fixed position different from the "normal position of use".
requirements.test_case: Place each movable component in each fixed position and measure the hidden portion of the apparent surface; pass if ≤ 50 %.

requirements.text: If the 50 per cent requirement is not practicable, additional lamps satisfying all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for rear position lamps and retro-reflectors shall be switched ON when the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of these lamps is more than 50 per cent hidden by the movable component.
requirements.test_case: With the movable component in such position, verify additional compliant lamps switch ON.

requirements.text: If more than 50 per cent of the apparent surface of the lamp in the direction of the reference axis can be hidden by the movable components, a notice in the vehicle shall inform the user that in certain position(s) of the movable components other road users shall be warned of the presence of the vehicle on the road, for example by means of a warning triangle or other devices according to national requirements for use on the road; this does not apply to retro-reflectors.
requirements.test_case: Check the vehicle documentation/notice for the required user warning when the movable component can hide more than 50 % of the lamp apparent surface.

requirements.text: With the exception of retro-reflectors, a lamp even bearing an approval mark is deemed not to be present when it cannot be made to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse.
requirements.test_case: Verify on the vehicle that the rear position, stop and reversing lamps operate without any action beyond installing a light source and/or fuse.

requirements.text: Lamps approved with light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 37, except when such light sources are used as non-replaceable light source(s), shall be fitted in a vehicle in such a way that the light source can be correctly replaced without the need for expert assistance and without the need for special tools, other than those provided with the vehicle by the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Replace the light source on the installed lamp using only vehicle-supplied tools and confirm correct replacement without expert assistance.

requirements.text: For lamps approved with replaceable light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 37, the vehicle manufacturer shall provide with the vehicle a detailed description of the procedure for replacement.
requirements.test_case: Check that the vehicle documentation contains a detailed light source replacement procedure.

requirements.text: In the case where a light source module includes a holder for an approved replaceable light source according to Regulation No. 37, this light source shall be replaceable as required in paragraph 5.23.
requirements.test_case: Verify the R37 light source in the module can be replaced per paragraph 5.23 without special tools.

requirements.text: Any temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of a rear position lamp shall be similar in colour, main intensity and position to the function that has ceased to operate and the replacement device shall remain operational in its original safety function.
requirements.test_case: Simulate failure of the rear position lamp and verify the replacement function has similar colour, intensity and position while the replacement device keeps its original function.

requirements.text: During temporary fail-safe replacement of the rear position lamp function, a tell-tale on the dashboard shall indicate occurrence of a temporary replacement and need for repair.
requirements.test_case: Simulate failure and verify the dashboard tell-tale indicates temporary replacement and need for repair.

requirements.text: For rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control, the intensity of all such lamps, when combined, grouped or reciprocally incorporated, shall vary all together in the same manner and in a similar proportion.
requirements.test_case: Vary the intensity control conditions and measure that R2 and S2 intensities change together in the same manner and similar proportion.

requirements.text: For rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control, in the entire intensity range, the specific prescribed ratio between the luminous intensities of two lamps, if applicable, shall be maintained throughout variation transitions.
requirements.test_case: Measure stop/position intensity ratio across the full variation range and transitions and confirm the prescribed ratio is maintained.

requirements.text: For R2 rear position lamps and S2 stop lamps with variable luminous intensity, increase and decrease of the luminous intensity in relation to environmental conditions shall remain in the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations.
requirements.test_case: Verify intensity variation under the listed environmental conditions stays within R148 limits.

requirements.text: For R2 rear position lamps and S2 stop lamps with variable luminous intensity, a decrease of the luminous intensity related to traffic conditions, in the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations, is allowed only as long as the vehicle speed is equal or less than 20 km/h or the distance to the following vehicle is equal or less than 20 m, and an already activated decrease may remain active only as long as the vehicle speed is equal or less than 50 km/h.
requirements.test_case: Check control logic: decrease activates only at ≤20 km/h or ≤20 m following distance and is cancelled above 50 km/h.

requirements.text: For lamps with variable luminous intensity, no sharp variation of intensity shall be observed during transition.
requirements.test_case: Record luminous intensity during transitions and confirm no abrupt step changes.

requirements.text: For vehicles of M and N categories, when the electrical system of the vehicle is in a constant voltage operating condition, the voltage supplied at the terminals of devices which have been tested by the application of a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, or in a secondary operating mode or at a voltage requested by the applicant, shall not exceed the voltage specified for the relevant devices or functions as they have been approved.
requirements.test_case: Measure terminal voltage at constant vehicle voltage operating condition and confirm it does not exceed the approved voltage.

requirements.text: For vehicles of M and N categories, in all cases of electric power supply conditions not covered by paragraph 5.27.1., the voltage at the terminals of the device(s) or function(s) shall not exceed 6.75 V (6 Volt-Systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) or 28 V (24 Volt-Systems) by more than 3 per cent.
requirements.test_case: Measure the voltage at the lamp terminals at constant vehicle operating voltage and confirm it is ≤ 13.5 V +3 % for a 12 V system.

requirements.text: There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of the lamp observed from infinity, except obstacles already presented when the lamp was type-approved.
requirements.test_case: Check on the installed vehicle that no vehicle part obstructs the apparent surface within the required geometric visibility angles.

requirements.text: If measurements of geometric visibility are taken closer to the lamp, the direction of observation shall be shifted parallel to achieve the same accuracy.
requirements.test_case: Verify near-field visibility measurements use parallel-shifted observation directions.

requirements.text: If, when the lamp is installed, any part of the apparent surface of the lamp is hidden by any further parts of the vehicle, proof shall be furnished that the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles still conforms to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.
requirements.test_case: Photometrically measure the lamp with the obstruction simulated and confirm the prescribed values are still met.

requirements.text: In the case of an interdependent lamp system the geometric visibility requirements shall be fulfilled when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
requirements.test_case: Operate all interdependent lamps together and verify geometric visibility angles are met.

requirements.text: All lamps (devices) shall, where applicable, be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations as specified in the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 6 of this Regulation when installed on a vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Check the rear position, stop, reversing lamp and retro-reflector carry valid R148/R150 approval marks.

requirements.text: In case of light-signalling lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo, the lamp shall be type approved according to the requirements of the UN Regulation No. 148.
requirements.test_case: Verify the logo-bearing lamp holds an R148 approval covering the logo.

requirements.text: Lamps installed on a vehicle approved according to this Regulation and approved for one or more replaceable light source categories according to Regulations Nos. 37, 99 or 128 shall be fitted with light sources approved according to these light source categories only; this does not concern light source modules, LED modules and non-replaceable light sources, except when they are required to be approved by the applicable Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Inspect fitted light sources and confirm they carry approvals matching the lamp's approved categories.

requirements.text: Lamps equipped with LED substitute light source(s) shall be used only where the statement indicated in paragraph 3.2.8. is present and positive, and the presence of the marking on the lamps related to the use of LED substitute light source(s) shall be checked.
requirements.test_case: Check the vehicle documentation statement and the LED substitute marking on the lamp.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp shall be present (mandatory) on motor vehicles.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the M1 vehicle installation; pass if at least one reversing lamp is fitted.

requirements.text: On motor vehicles of category M1, one reversing lamp device is mandatory and a second device is optional.
requirements.test_case: Count reversing lamps installed on the M1 vehicle; pass if one or two devices are fitted.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp devices shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 23, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
requirements.test_case: Check the lamp carries a valid R23 or R148 approval mark for the reversing function; pass if present.

requirements.text: In height, the reversing lamp shall be not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground.
requirements.test_case: Measure apparent surface heights of the installed reversing lamp; pass if within 250 mm to 1,200 mm above ground.

requirements.text: In length, the reversing lamp shall be at the rear of the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Inspect installation; pass if the reversing lamp is located at the rear of the vehicle.

requirements.text: For reversing lamp devices installed at the rear of the vehicle, the geometric visibility defined by angles α and β, as specified in paragraph 2.10.7., shall be α = 15° upwards and 5° downwards, and β = 45° to right and to left if there is only one device.
requirements.test_case: Verify unobstructed visibility of the apparent surface over 15° up, 5° down and 45° left/right; pass if visible throughout.

requirements.text: For reversing lamp devices installed at the rear of the vehicle, the geometric visibility defined by angles α and β, as specified in paragraph 2.10.7., shall be α = 15° upwards and 5° downwards, and β = 45° outwards and 30° inwards if there are two devices.
requirements.test_case: Verify unobstructed visibility of each lamp's apparent surface over 15° up, 5° down, 45° outwards and 30° inwards; pass if visible throughout.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp shall be oriented rearwards.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the installed lamp reference axis; pass if directed rearwards.

requirements.text: The electrical connections of the reversing lamp shall be such that the lamp can be switched ON only if the reverse gear is engaged and if the device which controls the starting and stopping of the propulsion system is in such a position that operation of the propulsion system is possible.
requirements.test_case: Functional vehicle test with reverse gear and ignition states; pass if lamp lights only with reverse engaged and propulsion operable.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp shall not switch ON or remain ON if either the reverse gear is not engaged or the device which controls the starting and stopping of the propulsion system is not in a position where operation of the propulsion system is possible.
requirements.test_case: Disengage reverse gear or switch off propulsion while lamp is lit; pass if lamp switches OFF and cannot be switched ON.

requirements.text: Stop lamp devices of S1 or S2 categories are mandatory on all categories of vehicles (including M1).
requirements.test_case: Inspect the M1 vehicle installation and approval marking to confirm stop lamps of category S1 or S2 are fitted.

requirements.text: The stop lamp devices shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
requirements.test_case: Check the approval mark on the rear lamp and approval certificate for an S1/S2 stop lamp approval under R7 (02 or later) or R148 (00 or later).

requirements.text: Two S1 or S2 category stop lamp devices shall be installed on all categories of vehicles.
requirements.test_case: Count the S1/S2 stop lamp devices fitted on the vehicle (left and right rear lamps); pass if exactly two are present.

requirements.text: For M1 category vehicles, for S1 or S2 categories stop lamp devices, that point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Measure on the vehicle the lateral distance from the outermost point of the stop lamp apparent surface to the vehicle's extreme outer edge; pass if ≤ 400 mm.

requirements.text: For S1 or S2 categories stop lamp devices, the mounting height above the ground shall be not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed).
requirements.test_case: Measure the height of the stop lamp apparent surface above ground per paragraph 5.8.1; pass if between 350 mm and 1,500 mm (or 2,100 mm where justified by bodywork).

requirements.text: In length, S1 or S2 categories stop lamp devices shall be positioned at the rear of the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the vehicle installation; pass if the stop lamps are located at the rear of the vehicle.

requirements.text: For S1 or S2 categories stop lamp devices, the horizontal angle of geometric visibility shall be 45° to the left and to the right of the longitudinal axis of the vehicle; however, for stop lamps mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
requirements.test_case: Verify on the vehicle that the stop lamp apparent surface is unobstructed over 45° left and right (20° inward under H plane if mounted below 750 mm).

requirements.text: For S1 or S2 categories stop lamp devices, the vertical angle of geometric visibility shall be 15° above and below the horizontal; however, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
requirements.test_case: Verify on the vehicle that the stop lamp apparent surface is visible 15° above and below horizontal (5° downward if mounted below 750 mm).

requirements.text: The stop lamps shall be oriented towards the rear of the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Inspect installation; pass if the stop lamp reference axis points towards the rear of the vehicle.

requirements.text: All stop lamps shall be switched ON simultaneously when the braking system provides the relevant signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.
requirements.test_case: Apply the brake signal on the vehicle and observe; pass if all stop lamps switch ON simultaneously.

requirements.text: The rear position lamps of R or R1 or R2 categories shall be mandatory.
requirements.test_case: Inspect vehicle; pass if rear position lamps of category R, R1 or R2 are fitted.

requirements.text: In width, that point on the apparent surface of the rear position lamp in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Measure the lateral distance from the outermost point of the rear position lamp apparent surface to the vehicle extreme outer edge; pass if ≤ 400 mm.

requirements.text: In height, the rear position lamps shall be above the ground, not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed).
requirements.test_case: Measure the height of the rear position lamp apparent surface per paragraph 5.8.1; pass if between 350 mm and 1,500 mm (or 2,100 mm where justified).

requirements.text: In length, the rear position lamps shall be positioned at the rear of the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Inspect installation; pass if rear position lamps are at the rear of the vehicle.

requirements.text: The horizontal angle of geometric visibility of the rear position lamps shall be 45° inwards and 80° outwards; however, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
requirements.test_case: Verify on the vehicle that the rear position lamp apparent surface is visible from 45° inwards to 80° outwards (20° inward under H plane if below 750 mm).

requirements.text: The vertical angle of geometric visibility of the rear position lamps shall be 15° above and below the horizontal; however, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
requirements.test_case: Verify on the vehicle that the rear position lamp apparent surface is visible 15° above and below horizontal (5° downward if below 750 mm).

requirements.text: For M1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1., and only if a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, the geometric visibility of the rear position lamps shall be horizontal 45° outwards to 45° inwards (inward angle may be reduced to 20° under the H plane where mounted below 750 mm) and vertical 15° above and below the horizontal (downward angle may be reduced to 5° where mounted below 750 mm).
requirements.test_case: If the alternative is used, confirm rear side-marker lamp presence and verify visibility 45° out to 45° in and 15° up/down.

requirements.text: When the alternative geometric visibility of paragraph 6.10.5.2. is used, to be considered visible, the rear position lamp shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 square centimetres, excluding the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light.
requirements.test_case: Measure the unobstructed apparent surface at the boundary angles excluding non-transmitting retro-reflector area; pass if ≥ 12.5 cm².

requirements.text: The rear position lamps shall be oriented rearwards.
requirements.test_case: Inspect installation; pass if rear position lamp reference axis points rearwards.

requirements.text: The electrical connections of the rear position lamps shall be in accordance with paragraph 5.11.
requirements.test_case: Check the vehicle wiring and switching of the rear position lamps against paragraph 5.11 requirements.

requirements.text: A closed-circuit tell-tale for the rear position lamps is mandatory and it shall be combined with that of the front position lamps; this requirement does not apply when daytime running lamps are switched ON.
requirements.test_case: Switch on the rear position lamps on the vehicle and verify a closed-circuit tell-tale illuminates, shared with the front position lamp tell-tale.

requirements.text: For the rear position lamps, a tell-tale indicating failure is mandatory if required by the component Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Check the component Regulation requirements and simulate a rear position lamp failure to verify the failure tell-tale activates where required.

requirements.text: In all cases, the distance between the rear fog-lamp and each stop-lamp shall be greater than 100 mm.
requirements.test_case: Measure on the vehicle the distance between the rear fog lamp and each stop lamp of the rear lamp and verify it exceeds 100 mm.

requirements.text: The rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, is mandatory on motor vehicles.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the M1 vehicle and verify that non-triangular rear retro-reflectors are fitted.

requirements.text: The number of rear retro-reflectors, non-triangular, shall be two, type-approved according to the requirements concerning Class IA or IB retro-reflectors in the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3, or in the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150.
requirements.test_case: Verify two rear retro-reflectors are fitted and that each bears a Class IA or IB approval mark under R3 (02+) or R150 (00+).

requirements.text: Additional retro-reflecting devices and materials (including two retro-reflectors not complying with paragraph 6.14.4.) shall not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.
requirements.test_case: Inspect any additional retro-reflecting devices and verify they do not obstruct or impair the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.

requirements.text: In width, that point on the illuminating surface of the rear retro-reflector which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Measure the lateral distance from the outermost point of the retro-reflector illuminating surface to the vehicle's extreme outer edge and verify it is ≤ 400 mm.

requirements.text: In height, the rear retro-reflector shall be above the ground not less than 250 mm nor more than 900 mm (not more than 1,200 mm if grouped with any rear lamp(s), 1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm or 1,200 mm respectively).
requirements.test_case: Measure the mounting height of the retro-reflector above ground per paragraph 5.8 and verify it is between 250 mm and 900 mm (1,200 mm if grouped, 1,500 mm if bodywork prevents).

requirements.text: In length, the rear retro-reflector shall be at the rear of the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the vehicle and verify the retro-reflector is located at the rear of the vehicle.

requirements.text: The geometric visibility of the rear retro-reflector shall be a horizontal angle of 30° inwards and outwards.
requirements.test_case: Verify on the installed lamp that the retro-reflector is visible over 30° inwards and outwards horizontally.

requirements.text: The geometric visibility of the rear retro-reflector shall be a vertical angle of 10° above and below horizontal; however, where the retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 10° may be reduced to 5°.
requirements.test_case: Verify on the installed lamp that the retro-reflector is visible 10° above and 10° below horizontal (5° downward if mounted below 750 mm).

requirements.text: The orientation of the rear retro-reflector shall be rearwards.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the installed retro-reflector and verify its reference axis is directed rearwards.

requirements.text: Triangular rear retro-reflectors are prohibited on motor vehicles; the rear retro-reflector of the lamp shall not be triangular.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the retro-reflector shape and verify it is not triangular.

requirements.text: When daytime running lamps are switched ON, the rear position lamps shall be switched ON; however, the rear position lamps may be switched OFF when the daytime running lamps are switched ON, and may remain switched OFF as long as the ambient light conditions outside the vehicle are above 7,000 lux (measured according to the requirements of Annex 13).
requirements.test_case: On the vehicle, switch on the daytime running lamps under ambient light at or below 7,000 lux (Annex 13 method) and check that the rear position lamps are ON.

requirements.text: Conspicuity markings are prohibited on vehicles of category M1; the rear lamp intended for M1 vehicles shall not incorporate or be fitted with conspicuity markings.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp and its installation on the M1 vehicle; pass if no conspicuity marking (retro-reflective marking material) is fitted.

requirements.text: Where the emergency stop signal is provided by the stop lamps, the emergency stop signal shall be given by the simultaneous operation of all the stop lamps fitted as described in paragraph 6.23.7.
requirements.test_case: Trigger emergency braking on the vehicle and verify visually that all fitted stop lamps operate simultaneously.

requirements.text: Where the emergency stop signal is provided by the stop lamps, the number of lamps shall be as specified in paragraph 6.7.2.
requirements.test_case: Count the stop lamps used for the emergency stop signal on the vehicle and check against paragraph 6.7.2.

requirements.text: Where the emergency stop signal is provided by the stop lamps, the geometric visibility shall be as specified in paragraph 6.7.5.
requirements.test_case: Verify the angles of geometric visibility of the stop lamps on the vehicle against paragraph 6.7.5.

requirements.text: All the lamps of the emergency stop signal shall flash in phase at a frequency of 4.0 ± 1.0 Hz.
requirements.test_case: Activate the emergency stop signal and measure the flash frequency and phase of all lamps; pass if in phase and within 3.0-5.0 Hz.

requirements.text: If any of the lamps of the emergency stop signal to the rear of the vehicle use filament light sources, the frequency shall be 4.0 +0.0/-1.0 Hz.
requirements.test_case: Measure flash frequency of the emergency stop signal; pass if within 3.0-4.0 Hz.

requirements.text: The emergency stop signal shall operate independently of other lamps.
requirements.test_case: Activate the emergency stop signal with other lamps in various states and verify it operates independently.

requirements.text: The emergency stop signal shall be switched ON and OFF automatically.
requirements.test_case: Verify on the vehicle that the emergency stop signal activates and deactivates without manual control.

requirements.text: The emergency stop signal shall be switched ON only when the vehicle speed is above 50 km/h and the braking system is providing the emergency braking logic signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.
