requirements.test_case: Perform emergency braking above and below 50 km/h; pass if the signal activates only above 50 km/h with the emergency braking logic signal present.

requirements.text: The emergency stop signal shall be automatically switched OFF if the emergency braking logic signal as defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H is no longer provided or if the hazard warning signal is activated.
requirements.test_case: Remove the emergency braking logic signal and separately activate the hazard warning signal; pass if the emergency stop signal switches OFF in both cases.

requirements.text: If the lamps of the rear combination lamp (rear position lamp or reversing lamp) are used for the answer-back signal, the answer-back signal shall only operate under the park condition of a vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Activate the answer-back signal in park and in non-park vehicle states; pass if it operates only in the park condition.

requirements.text: If the answer-back signal provided by the lamps of the rear combination lamp flashes, the frequency shall not exceed 2.0 Hz.
requirements.test_case: Measure the flash frequency of the answer-back signal; pass if it does not exceed 2.0 Hz.

requirements.text: The answer-back signal shall be provided by approved lighting and light-signalling devices where the maximum luminous intensity per lamp does not exceed 700 cd on or above the HH line; stop lamps are not permitted to be used for the answer-back signal.
requirements.test_case: Verify the lamp used is approved and not the stop lamp, and measure intensity in answer-back mode; pass if it does not exceed 700 cd on or above the HH line.

requirements.text: The answer-back signal provided by the lamps of the rear combination lamp may only be activated automatically in conjunction with the locking and unlocking of the door(s) and/or the detection of the vehicle user in proximity to the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Check activation triggers of the answer-back signal; pass if it is activated only by door locking/unlocking and/or user proximity detection.

requirements.text: The duration of the optical indication of the answer-back signal provided by the lamps of the rear combination lamp shall not exceed 3 seconds, irrespective of whether it contains flashes, variations of intensity or variations in apparent surface.
requirements.test_case: Time the answer-back signal from beginning to end; pass if the duration does not exceed 3 s.

requirements.text: For verifying the visibility of a red lamp to the front (see paragraph 5.10.4.), the zone 1 explored by the eye of the observer shall be bounded in height by two horizontal planes 1 m and 2.2 m above the ground, and in width by a vertical plane forming to the front an angle of 15° outwards from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane, passing through the point or points of contact of vertical planes parallel to the vehicle's median longitudinal plane delimiting the vehicle's overall width; if there are several points of contact, the foremost shall correspond to the forward plane.
requirements.test_case: On the vehicle, observe from zone 1 (1 m to 2.2 m height, 15° outwards forward plane) and verify that no direct light from the red rear position and stop lamps is visible.

requirements.text: For verifying the visibility of a white lamp to the rear (see paragraph 5.10.4.), the zone 2 explored by the eye of the observer shall be bounded in height by two horizontal planes 1 m and 2.2 m above the ground, and in width by a vertical plane forming to the rear an angle of 15° outwards from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane, passing through the point or points of contact of vertical planes parallel to the vehicle's median longitudinal plane delimiting the vehicle's overall width; if there are several points of contact, the rearmost shall correspond to the rearward plane.
requirements.test_case: On the vehicle, observe from zone 2 (1 m to 2.2 m height, 15° outwards rearward plane) and verify white light to the rear is only from permitted lamps such as the reversing lamp.

requirements.text: The values measured for the distances of the position of the lamps in width, in height and in length, checked in accordance with paragraphs 2.10.2., 2.10.3., 2.10.4., 2.3.3. and 5.4., shall be such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled.
requirements.test_case: Measure the lamp position in width, height and length on the vehicle and confirm that each value meets the individual specification for the rear position, stop and reversing lamps and the retro-reflector.

requirements.text: The values measured for the angles of geometric visibility, checked in accordance with paragraph 2.10.7., shall be such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled, except that the limits of the angles may have an allowance corresponding to the ±3º variation permitted in paragraph 5.3. for the mounting of the light-signalling devices.
requirements.test_case: Measure the geometric visibility angles of each function on the vehicle and confirm they meet the individual specifications within the ±3° allowance.

requirements.text: The visibility of red light towards the front and of white light towards the rear shall be checked in accordance with paragraph 5.10.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the vehicle according to paragraph 5.10 and confirm that no red light from the lamp is visible towards the front and that no prohibited white light is visible towards the rear.

requirements.text: When every lamp supplied by the electrical system of the vehicle is switched on, the lamps and tell-tales shall function in accordance with the provisions set out in paragraphs 5.11. to 5.14. and with the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.
requirements.test_case: Switch on each function (position, stop, reversing) and confirm that the lamp and the related tell-tale operate as required by paragraphs 5.11 to 5.14 and the individual specifications.

requirements.text: The presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, the category of lamps, checked by visual inspection of the lamps and their markings, shall be such that the requirements set out in paragraphs 5.15. and 5.16. as well as in the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the lamps and their approval markings and confirm that presence, number, colour, arrangement and category comply with paragraphs 5.15 and 5.16 and the individual specifications.

requirements.text: When two or more lamps are part of the same unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps (rear position, stop and reversing lamps), each of these lamps shall satisfy the provisions set out in this Regulation or in another Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Verify that each function in the combination lamp has a passing test report against R148 (or the relevant Regulation).

requirements.text: Lamps not satisfying the provisions of any of those Regulations shall not be part of the unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps.
requirements.test_case: Review the BOM and function list to confirm that no non-compliant or non-approved lamp function is integrated in the housing.

requirements.text: All the devices of an interdependent lamp system must be submitted for type approval by the same applicant.
requirements.test_case: Check the approval application to confirm that all interdependent lamps are submitted by the same applicant.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp shall be identified by the symbol R1 (steady) or R2 (variable) as listed in Table 1.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the R1 or R2 symbol, consistent with the steady or variable intensity design.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp shall be identified by the symbol AR (the letters A and R may be mingled) as listed in Table 1.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the AR symbol.

requirements.text: Every device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the drawing and sample for a marking space large enough for all required markings.

requirements.text: All markings shall be clearly legible and indelible.
requirements.test_case: Visually check legibility, then rub the markings (e.g. with a solvent-soaked cloth) and confirm that they remain legible.

requirements.text: With regard to the size of the approval marking, the value for "a" shall be at least 5 mm.
requirements.test_case: Measure dimension "a" of the approval mark and confirm that it is ≥ 5 mm.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for a circle with E and the country number.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall consist of the four to six-digit sequential number, being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for a 4-6 digit sequential number matching the approval number.

requirements.text: The sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
requirements.test_case: Visually confirm that the sequential number is adjacent to the E-circle.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall consist of the symbols identifying the light signalling lamps prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for symbols matching each approved function (e.g. R1/R2, S1/S2, AR).

requirements.text: The approval marking shall consist of the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for "148R" followed by the series digits (e.g. 148R01).

requirements.text: On lamps which cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, the approval marking shall include a horizontal arrow showing in which position the lamp is to be mounted.
requirements.test_case: For handed lamps, inspect the marking for a horizontal arrow indicating the mounting position.

requirements.text: The arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle in the case of rear position lamps.
requirements.test_case: Confirm that the arrow on the handed rear position lamp points outboard when the lamp is installed.

requirements.text: The arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle in the case of reversing lamps in case of reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps.
requirements.test_case: Confirm that the arrow on the reversing lamp with reduced light distribution points outboard.

requirements.text: If applicable, the additional letter "D" shall be placed to the right side of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4. on lamps which may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps.
requirements.test_case: Inspect for the letter D to the right of the function symbol.

requirements.text: On lamps with reduced light distribution (see paragraph 1.1. of Annex 3), the approval marking shall include a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for a downward vertical arrow from a horizontal segment.

requirements.text: Lamps shall bear the approval marking.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the presence of the complete approval marking.

requirements.text: Lamps shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the applicant's trade name or mark.

requirements.text: Lamps, with the exception of lamps with non-replaceable light sources, shall bear a marking indicating the category or categories of light source(s) prescribed.
requirements.test_case: For a lamp with replaceable light sources, inspect for the light source category marking.

requirements.text: In the case where the lamp has been approved for LED substitute light source(s), the lamp shall also bear a marking indicating the category or categories of the LED substitute light source(s).
requirements.test_case: Inspect for the LED substitute light source category marking.

requirements.text: Lamps shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage, in the case of lamps with an electronic light source control gear, a variable luminous intensity control, a secondary operating mode and/or non-replaceable light sources.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the rated voltage or voltage range marking (e.g. 12V).

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant, the specific identification code of the module (starting letters "MD" followed by the approval mark without the circle) and the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
requirements.test_case: Inspect each module for the trade name, the MD identification code and the rated voltage.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module and the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the module identification code and the rated voltage.

requirements.text: An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control being part of the lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the external control gear for its identification number and the manufacturer name.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp which is not designed to be separated from the transparent part of the lamp emitting the light.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the marking location is on a part that is not separable from the light-emitting lens.

requirements.text: The approval marking, as well as the category or categories of LED substitute light source(s) prescribed, if any, shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood or boot lid or a door is opened.
requirements.test_case: With the lamp installed on the vehicle (movable parts opened if needed), confirm that the marking is visible.

requirements.text: If the outer lens of a device is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on both the detachable lens and the main body.
requirements.test_case: For a detachable lens, inspect both the lens and the body for the approval marking.

requirements.text: In case an outer lens is used for several devices and bears different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
requirements.test_case: Inspect each device body and confirm that it carries only its own function markings.

requirements.text: The approval marking and the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.2., 3.3.3.3., 3.3.3.4., 3.3.3.5. (b) and 3.3.3.6. shall be affixed on the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp and confirm that all of these markings are affixed to it.

requirements.text: The markings in paragraph 3.3.3.5.(a) shall be affixed on the light source module component.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the module component for the 3.3.3.5(a) markings.

requirements.text: Where a single approval mark is affixed to the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, the marking shall be visible after their installation.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp installed on the vehicle (or in its mounting position) and confirm the single approval mark is visible.

requirements.text: Where a single approval mark is affixed to the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of the lamps that transmits light can be removed without at the same time removing the approval mark.
requirements.test_case: Review the design and disassembly: confirm every light-transmitting part (e.g. outer lens) carries or cannot be removed without the approval mark.

requirements.text: The size of the components of a single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
requirements.test_case: Measure the characters of the single approval mark and compare with the minimum sizes of the pertinent Regulations.

requirements.text: Each lamp submitted for approval shall conform to the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5.
requirements.test_case: Verify via the type approval test report that all paragraph 4 and 5 requirements are passed for each lamp function.

requirements.text: The requirements contained in sections 5 "General specifications" and 6 "Individual specifications" (and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections) of UN Regulation No. 48 and its series of amendments in force at the time of application for the lamp type approval shall apply, the requirements pertinent to each lamp and to the category/ies of vehicle on which the lamp is intended to be installed being applied where its verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.
requirements.test_case: Check the R48 sections 5 and 6 provisions verifiable at lamp level (e.g. geometric visibility, colours) for the rear position, stop and reversing lamps on M1.

requirements.text: The lamps must be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which they may be subjected in such use, their satisfactory operation remains assured and they retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Perform vibration/durability testing and re-measure photometry and colour; confirm operation and characteristics remain within limits.

requirements.text: In the case of a rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp, these functions shall either be provided by multiple light sources (for instance, a double filament light source) or be intended for use in a vehicle equipped with a tell-tale indicating failure for the lamps.
requirements.test_case: Review the circuit design to confirm multiple light sources are used or the lamp is declared for vehicles with a failure tell-tale.

requirements.text: Stop lamps and reversing lamps shall not incorporate a logo.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the stop and reversing lamp apparent surfaces and confirm no logo is incorporated.

requirements.text: If a manufacturer logo is incorporated, the enclosed light emitting surface of the logo (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 100 cm2.
requirements.test_case: Measure the projected logo light-emitting surface along the reference axis and confirm it is ≤ 100 cm2.

requirements.text: If a manufacturer logo is incorporated in the rear position lamp, only the logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or the body manufacturer is allowed.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the logo and the applicant statement to confirm it is the vehicle or body manufacturer brand logo only.

requirements.text: In a single lamp containing more than one light source, a group of light sources, wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light, shall be considered to be one light source.
requirements.test_case: Review the LED wiring schematic and identify light-source groups considered as one light source for failure assessment.

requirements.text: In case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source, either the light intensity shall comply with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3 and when all light sources are illuminated the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded, or a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in UN Regulation No. 48, shall be produced.
requirements.test_case: Simulate failure of each light source and measure intensities against Annex 3 minima, or verify a failure tell-tale signal is produced.

requirements.text: In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a rear position lamp category R2 or a stop lamp category S2 emitting more than the maximum value of category R1 or S1 respectively, requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.
requirements.test_case: Simulate variable intensity control failure and confirm intensities fall automatically within R1/S1 steady limits.

requirements.text: The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light source(s) approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128, provided that no restriction on the use is made at the time of application for type approval, and/or light source module(s) and/or non-replaceable light source(s).
requirements.test_case: Review the BOM to confirm all light sources are R37/R99/R128 approved, light source modules or non-replaceable light sources.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the design of the lamp shall be such that the light source(s) can be fixed in no other position but the correct one.
requirements.test_case: Attempt to fit the light source in alternative orientations; confirm only the correct position is possible.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the light source(s) holder shall conform to the characteristics given in IEC Publication 60061, the holder data sheet relevant to the category of light source(s) prescribed (and of any LED substitute light source category also prescribed) applying.
requirements.test_case: Gauge the holder against the IEC 60061 data sheet for the prescribed light source category.

requirements.text: Light Signalling Devices shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances, which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Perform EMC emission tests (e.g. per UN R10) and confirm no disturbance causing malfunction of other vehicle systems.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that it can only be fitted in the designated and correct position and can only be removed with the use of tool(s).
requirements.test_case: Attempt incorrect fitment and tool-less removal; confirm both are impossible.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that it is tamperproof.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the module design to confirm it cannot be opened or altered without destruction.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), regardless of the use of tool(s), the light source module shall not be interchangeable with any replaceable UN approved light source and/or any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics that is located in the same lamp housing.
requirements.test_case: Attempt to interchange modules and UN approved light sources within the housing; confirm not possible.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), when the light source module is removed and replaced by another module provided by the applicant and bearing the same light source module identification code, the photometric requirements of the device shall be met.
requirements.test_case: Replace the module with another of the same identification code and re-measure photometry against the limits.

requirements.text: All measurements, photometric and colorimetric, shall be made with respect to the conditions of paragraph 4.8., the particulars of the methods of measurement being given in Annex 3.
requirements.test_case: Review the test report to confirm photometric and colorimetric measurements followed paragraph 4.8 and Annex 3 methods.

requirements.text: In the case of replaceable UN approved light sources, all measurements shall be made using standard light sources as specified in R.E.5.
requirements.test_case: Confirm the test report records use of R.E.5 standard light sources for measurements.

requirements.text: In the case of replaceable UN approved light source(s) controlled by an electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control, the standard light source(s) shall have a luminous flux value that does not deviate more than 5 per cent from its reference/objective luminous flux value when test voltage is applied.
requirements.test_case: Measure the luminous flux of the standard light sources at test voltage and confirm deviation from reference flux is ≤5 %.

requirements.text: In the case of a lamp equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), all measurements shall be made with the light source(s) present in the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Verify in the test report that photometric and colorimetric measurements were made with the LED modules installed in the lamp.

requirements.text: In case of a lamp (function) using light sources which are subject to more than one of the conditions prescribed in paragraph 4.8., the photometric measurements shall be made separately, in accordance with each applicable condition(s) set forth in paragraph 4.8.
requirements.test_case: Check that each light-source group was measured separately under its applicable condition.

requirements.text: In case of a lamp (function) using light sources which are subject to more than one of the conditions prescribed in paragraph 4.8., all separate measurement results shall be added together.
requirements.test_case: Verify the reported intensities are the sum of the separate measurements.

requirements.text: During photometric measurements, stray reflections shall be avoided by appropriate masking.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the goniophotometer set-up for masking that prevents stray reflections during measurement.

requirements.text: In the case where the lamp may be installed on the vehicle in more than one or in a field of different positions the photometric measurements shall be repeated for each position or for the extreme positions of the field of the reference axis specified by the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Confirm photometric measurements were repeated at each declared position or at extreme positions of the reference axis field.

requirements.text: In the case where the lamp, at the discretion of the applicant, also has to be approved with LED substitute light source(s), all measurements, photometric and colorimetric, shall be repeated using the LED substitute light source(s) prescribed.
requirements.test_case: Repeat photometric and colorimetric tests with the LED substitute light sources and verify compliance.

requirements.text: In the case of a lamp which is intended to be mounted inside the vehicle, a sample plate or sample plates (in case of different possibilities) as supplied shall be positioned in front of the lamp to be tested, in the geometrical position(s) as described in the application drawing(s).
requirements.test_case: Verify the supplied sample plate is positioned in front of the lamp during testing per the drawing.

requirements.text: If not otherwise specified, the intensities shall be measured with the light source continuously lit.
requirements.test_case: Verify the light sources are continuously lit during intensity measurement.

requirements.text: In case the results of measurements should be challenged, the distance of measurement shall be such that the law of the inverse of the square of the distance is applicable.
requirements.test_case: Check the measurement distance is sufficient for the inverse-square law to apply.

requirements.text: In case the results of measurements should be challenged, the measuring equipment shall be such that the angular aperture of the receiver viewed from the reference centre of the light is comprised between 10' and 1 degree.
requirements.test_case: Verify the receiver angular aperture from the reference centre is between 10' and 1°.

requirements.text: In case the results of measurements should be challenged, the intensity requirement for a particular direction of observation shall be deemed to be satisfied if that requirement is met in a direction deviating by not more than one-quarter of a degree from the direction of observation.
requirements.test_case: Evaluate disputed points within ±0.25° of the nominal direction and confirm compliance.

requirements.text: The limits of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of a light-signalling lamp shall be determined.
requirements.test_case: Determine and document the apparent surface limits of each function in the reference axis direction.

requirements.text: Unless otherwise specified, the voltage supplied at the lamp for testing shall be either 6.75 V (6 Volt-Systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) or 28 V (24 Volt-Systems).
requirements.test_case: Measure the supply voltage at the lamp terminals during testing and confirm 13.5 V (12 V system) or as applicable.

requirements.text: In case of a lamp controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Operate the lamp per the applicant's declared conditions and verify the test report records them.

requirements.text: In case of a lamp not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, in the case of light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s) the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Operate the lamp per applicant specification and verify the test report records it.

requirements.text: In case of a lamp not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, in the case of replaceable UN approved light source(s) the light sources shall be operated at the reference/objective luminous flux or alternatively at a different luminous flux with a proportional correction on the measured luminous intensities.
requirements.test_case: Verify the light sources are operated at reference flux or that intensities are proportionally corrected.

requirements.text: In case of lamps equipped with multiple replaceable UN approved light sources, the light sources shall be operated at a voltage or electrical current setting such that the actual luminous fluxes of the light sources do not deviate by more than 5 per cent from the average luminous flux of the light sources, and the measured luminous intensities shall be corrected proportionally for the difference between the average luminous flux and the applicable reference/objective luminous flux.
requirements.test_case: Check flux of each light source is within 5 % of the average and intensities are proportionally corrected.

requirements.text: If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, on the reference axis (HV), be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Measure HV intensity of both samples for each function and confirm it is not below the paragraph 5 minimum.

requirements.text: If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, in no direction where the lamp is visible, exceed the maximum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Scan the visible field of both samples and confirm no point exceeds the paragraph 5 maximum.

requirements.text: If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, outside the reference axis, be not less than the product of the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5. by the percentage specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question, or be not less than the intensity value as specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question.
requirements.test_case: Measure each grid point of the Annex 3 light distribution figure and confirm values meet minimum × percentage or the specified value.

requirements.text: If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2, be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Measure intensity across the Annex 2 geometric visibility angles and confirm it is not below the specified minimum.

requirements.text: The provisions of the relevant paragraphs of Annex 3 on local variations of intensity shall be observed.
requirements.test_case: Evaluate the light distribution for local intensity variations against Annex 3 provisions.

requirements.text: When an assembly of two independent lamps, to be type approved as lamps marked "D" and having the same function, is deemed to be a single lamp, it shall comply with the requirements for maximum intensity if all lamps together are lit.
requirements.test_case: Light both lamps together and confirm intensity does not exceed the maximum.

requirements.text: When an assembly of two independent lamps, to be type approved as lamps marked "D" and having the same function, is deemed to be a single lamp, it shall comply with the requirements for minimum intensity if either lamp has failed.
requirements.test_case: Disable each lamp in turn and confirm the remaining lamp meets minimum intensity.

requirements.text: An interdependent lamp system shall meet the requirements when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
requirements.test_case: Operate all interdependent lamps together and verify photometric and colorimetric compliance.

requirements.text: If the interdependent lamp system providing the rear position lamp is partly mounted on the fixed component and partly mounted on a movable component, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the applicant shall meet the outboard geometric visibility colorimetric and photometric requirement, at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).
requirements.test_case: Test the specified interdependent lamps at all fixed positions of the movable component for outboard visibility, colour and photometry.

requirements.text: The variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities outside the range specified in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Operate the variable intensity control across its range and confirm intensities stay within paragraph 5 limits.

requirements.text: The variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities exceeding the respective steady luminous intensity maximum specified in paragraph 5. for the specific lamp: (a) for systems depending only on daytime and night-time conditions: under night-time conditions; (b) for other systems: under standard conditions.
requirements.test_case: Under night-time or standard conditions, confirm intensity does not exceed the steady-lamp maximum.

requirements.text: If a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp producing either steady or variable luminous intensity, the ratio between the luminous intensities actually measured of the two lamps when turned on simultaneously and the intensity of the rear position lamp when turned on alone should be at least 5:1 in the field delimited by the straight horizontal lines passing through ±5° V and the straight vertical lines passing through ±10° H of the light distribution table.
requirements.test_case: Measure combined and position-only intensities within ±5° V / ±10° H and confirm ratio ≥5:1 at each point.

requirements.text: Tests for compliance of the luminous intensities shall be carried out according to Annex 8.
requirements.test_case: Verify luminous intensity tests followed the Annex 8 procedure.

requirements.text: The colour of the light emitted shall be measured inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in the relevant paragraph of Annex 3.
requirements.test_case: Measure chromaticity of each function within its Annex 3 light distribution grid.

requirements.text: Outside the field of the light distribution grid no sharp variation of colour shall be observed.
requirements.test_case: Visually/colorimetrically inspect outside the grid field and confirm no sharp colour variation.

requirements.text: To check the colorimetric characteristics, the test procedure described in paragraph 4.8. shall be applied.
requirements.test_case: Verify colorimetric tests used the paragraph 4.8 test conditions.

requirements.text: For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources, the colorimetric characteristics should be verified with the light sources present in the lamp, in accordance with relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 4.8.
requirements.test_case: Confirm colour measurements were made with the LED sources installed in the lamp.

requirements.text: For lamps (functions) using different light source technologies, the colorimetric characteristics shall be checked for each light source technology separately according to the applicable provisions in paragraphs 4.8.1. and 4.8.2.
requirements.test_case: Measure colour separately for each light source technology and confirm compliance.

requirements.text: For rear position lamps of category R1 (steady), the light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 4∙10^0 cd, a maximum luminous intensity of 1.7∙10^1 cd when used as a single lamp or 8.5∙10^0 cd when used as a lamp marked "D", a standard light distribution according to Figure A3-I, and a minimum luminous intensity of 5∙10^-2 cd within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1, as specified in Table 4.
requirements.test_case: Measure both samples: HV ≥4 cd, max ≤17 cd (8.5 cd if "D"), Figure A3-I grid compliant, ≥0.05 cd within Table A2-1 angles.

requirements.text: For rear position lamps of category R2 (variable), the light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 4∙10^0 cd, a maximum luminous intensity of 4.2∙10^1 cd when used as a single lamp or 2.1∙10^1 cd when used as a lamp marked "D", a standard light distribution according to Figure A3-I, and a minimum luminous intensity of 5∙10^-2 cd within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1, as specified in Table 4.
requirements.test_case: Measure both samples: HV ≥4 cd, max ≤42 cd (21 cd if "D"), Figure A3-I grid compliant, ≥0.05 cd within Table A2-1 angles.

requirements.text: For rear position lamps reciprocally incorporated with stop lamps, a luminous intensity of up to 6.0∙10^1 cd shall be permitted only below a plane forming an angle of 5° with and downward from the horizontal plane.
requirements.test_case: Confirm intensities above the Table 4 maximum (up to 60 cd) occur only below 5° down.

requirements.text: The minimum luminous intensity of the rear position lamp within the angles of geometric visibility shall be as specified in Table 4 (5∙10^-2 cd).
requirements.test_case: Measure across Table A2-1 geometric visibility angles and confirm ≥0.05 cd.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp shall meet the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
requirements.test_case: Assess the rear position lamp against paragraph 4.6 failure provisions.

requirements.text: The colour of light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
requirements.test_case: Measure chromaticity of the rear position lamp and confirm it lies within the red colour boundaries.

requirements.text: For a stop lamp of category S1 (steady), the minimum luminous intensity shall be 6.0∙10^1 cd, the maximum luminous intensity shall be 2.60∙10^2 cd when used as a single lamp or 1.30∙10^2 cd when used as a lamp marked "D", the standard light distribution shall be as defined in Figure A3-I and the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility (Table A2-1) shall be 3∙10^-1 cd, as given in Table 7.
requirements.test_case: Measure intensity in reference axis, standard light distribution points and geometric visibility field; verify ≥60 cd, ≤260 cd (≤130 cd if 'D'), and ≥0.3 cd within Table A2-1 angles.

requirements.text: For a stop lamp of category S2 (variable), the minimum luminous intensity shall be 6.0∙10^1 cd, the maximum luminous intensity shall be 7.30∙10^2 cd when used as a single lamp or 3.65∙10^2 cd when used as a lamp marked "D", the standard light distribution shall be as defined in Figure A3-I and the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility (Table A2-1) shall be 3∙10^-1 cd (day) and 7∙10^-2 cd (night), as given in Table 7.
requirements.test_case: Measure in day and night modes; verify ≥60 cd, ≤730 cd (≤365 cd if 'D'), and ≥0.3 cd day / ≥0.07 cd night within Table A2-1 angles.

requirements.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of the stop lamp shall meet the requirements in Table 7.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of both samples per Table 7; all values within the stated limits.

requirements.text: For a stop lamp of category S3 (steady), the minimum luminous intensity shall be 2.5∙10^1 cd, the maximum luminous intensity shall be 1.10∙10^2 cd when used as a single lamp or 5.5∙10^1 cd when used as a lamp marked "D", the standard light distribution shall be as defined in Figure A3-III and the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility (Table A2-1) shall be 3∙10^-1 cd, as given in Table 7.
requirements.test_case: Measure per Figure A3-III; verify ≥25 cd, ≤110 cd (≤55 cd if 'D'), ≥0.3 cd within geometric visibility.

requirements.text: The colour of light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of stop lamp light; chromaticity within red boundaries.

requirements.text: For a reversing lamp of category AR, the minimum luminous intensity shall be 8.0∙10^1 cd, with the standard light distribution as defined in Figure A3-V, as given in Table 10.
requirements.test_case: Measure in reference axis and Figure A3-V points; verify minimum ≥80 cd per distribution.

requirements.text: For a reversing lamp of category AR, the maximum luminous intensity in or above the H-plane shall be 3.00∙10^2 cd, as given in Table 10.
requirements.test_case: Measure intensity in and above H-plane; verify ≤300 cd.

requirements.text: For a reversing lamp of category AR, the maximum luminous intensity below the H-plane, down to 5°D, shall be 6.00∙10^2 cd, as given in Table 10.
requirements.test_case: Measure intensity between H-plane and 5°D; verify ≤600 cd.

requirements.text: In the case where the reversing lamp is intended to be installed on a vehicle exclusively in a pair of devices, the photometric intensity may be verified only up to an angle of 30° inwards where a photometric value of at least 2.5∙10^1 cd shall be satisfied, and this condition shall be clearly explained in the application for approval.
requirements.test_case: Measure intensity up to 30° inwards; verify ≥25 cd.

requirements.text: The colour of light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of reversing lamp light through the lens zone; chromaticity within white boundaries.

requirements.text: The singular rear position lamp (MR) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 80° inboard / 80° outboard and minimum vertical angles of 15° above / 10° below (15°/5° for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm), as given in Table A2-1.
requirements.test_case: Verify on a goniometer that the apparent surface is visible over 80°/80° horizontally and 15°/10° vertically, or 15°/5° below 750 mm.

requirements.text: The rear position lamps (MR) installed as a pair shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 20° inboard / 80° outboard and minimum vertical angles of 15° above / 10° below (15°/5° for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm), as given in Table A2-1.
requirements.test_case: Verify on a goniometer that the apparent surface is visible over 20°/80° horizontally and 15°/10° vertically, or 15°/5° below 750 mm.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp (R1, R2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard / 80° outboard (20°/80° reduced angles used only below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm). It shall have minimum vertical angles of 15° above / 15° below (15°/5° for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm; 5°/15° for optional lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of more than 2,100 mm), as given in Table A2-1.
requirements.test_case: Measure the geometric visibility of the rear position lamp apparent surface on a goniometer and confirm it is unobstructed over at least 45°/80° horizontally and 15°/15° vertically, or the reduced angles applicable to the mounting height.

requirements.text: The singular stop lamp (MS) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard / 45° outboard and minimum vertical angles of 15° above / 10° below (15°/5° for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm), as given in Table A2-1.
requirements.test_case: Verify on a goniometer that the apparent surface is visible over 45°/45° horizontally and 15°/10° vertically, or 15°/5° below 750 mm.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp shall meet, for the various directions of measurement relative to the reference axis (H = 0°, V = 0°, passing through the centre of reference), the minimum intensities given in Figures A3-I to A3-XV as a percentage of the minimum intensities required, mathematically rounded down to three significant digits, unless specified otherwise.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement at each grid direction; each measured intensity ≥ the figure percentage × required minimum, rounded down to three significant digits.

requirements.text: Where the rear position lamp or the stop lamp of category S1, S2 or MS is intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
requirements.test_case: Check manufacturer-declared mounting height; if ≤ 750 mm, verify that photometric compliance is demonstrated down to 5° below horizontal.

requirements.text: Within the field of light distribution schematically shown as a grid, the light intensity in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value being shown on the grid lines surrounding the questioned direction as a percentage.
requirements.test_case: Scan intensities between grid points; each value ≥ the lowest minimum percentage on surrounding grid lines.

requirements.text: In the case of reversing lamps, if visual examination of the lamp appears to reveal substantial local variations of intensity, a check shall be made to ensure that no intensity measured between two of the directions of measurement is below 50 per cent of the lower minimum intensity of the two prescribed for these directions of measurement.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect reversing lamp; if local variations seen, measure between adjacent measurement directions and confirm ≥ 50% of the lower prescribed minimum.

requirements.text: The rear position lamps and stop lamps of category S1 or S2 shall meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I, the values shown giving, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities as a percentage of the minimum intensities required (see Tables 4 and 7).
requirements.test_case: Measure rear position and stop lamp intensities at Figure A3-I points; each ≥ given percentage of the table minimum.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp shall meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-V, the values shown giving, for the various directions of measurement relative to the axis of reference, the minimum intensities in cd.
requirements.test_case: Measure reversing lamp intensities at each Figure A3-V point; each ≥ the cd value shown.

requirements.text: The conformity requirements shall be considered satisfied from a mechanical and a geometric standpoint, in accordance with the requirements of this Regulation, if any, if the differences of the lamp do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations.
requirements.test_case: Compare mechanical and geometric features of randomly sampled production lamps with the approved type; pass if differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations.

requirements.text: With respect to photometric performance, when testing the photometric performances set forth in paragraph 4.8. of this Regulation of any lamp chosen at random, no measured value shall deviate from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3. of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Measure photometric performance of randomly chosen production rear position, stop and reversing lamps per paragraph 4.8.; pass if no value deviates from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3.

requirements.text: In the case of a lamp equipped with a replaceable light source, if results of the photometric test do not meet the requirements, tests on lamps shall be repeated using another standard light source.
requirements.test_case: If a lamp with replaceable light source fails photometry, repeat the photometric test with another standard light source and check compliance.

requirements.text: The chromaticity coordinates of the lamp shall be complied with when tested under conditions of paragraph 4.9. of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Measure chromaticity coordinates of the red (position, stop) and white (reversing) light of sampled lamps under paragraph 4.9. conditions; pass if within the prescribed colour boundaries.

requirements.text: For lamps (functions) using incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured after photometric stability shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
requirements.test_case: Operate the lamp until photometric stability and measure luminous intensities at all test points; all values must be within the minimum and maximum limits.

requirements.text: For reversing lamps using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
requirements.test_case: Measure reversing lamp intensities after 1 min and after 10 min of operation (directly or by HV ratio scaling from the stabilised distribution); all points must be within the min/max limits.

requirements.text: For rear position lamps and stop lamps using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
requirements.test_case: Measure rear position and stop lamp intensities after 1 min and after 30 min or photometric stability (directly or by HV ratio scaling); all points must be within the min/max limits.

requirements.text: For the rear position lamp, the luminous intensity distribution shall, in addition to paragraph 1, be checked for compliance at 4 seconds after switch ON, using HV as reference coordinate, as listed in Table A8-1.
requirements.test_case: Measure HV intensity 4 s after switch ON and scale the distribution by the HV ratio; all test points must meet the rear position lamp min/max limits.

requirements.text: For the reversing lamp, the luminous intensity distribution shall, in addition to paragraph 1, be checked for compliance at 0.2 seconds after switch ON, using HV as reference coordinate, as listed in Table A8-1.
requirements.test_case: Measure HV intensity 0.2 s after switch ON and scale the distribution by the HV ratio; all test points must meet the reversing lamp min/max limits.

requirements.text: In case a lamp (function) uses LED technology only, the lamp (function) is deemed to comply with the corresponding intensity requirements at all points in time, if the values measured according to paragraph 1.2. are compliant.
requirements.test_case: Confirm all lamp functions use LED technology only and that measurements per paragraph 1.2 are compliant; additional time-point testing then not required.

requirements.text: In case a lamp (function) uses any other light generating technology, the corresponding intensity requirements of the lamp (function) shall be tested and checked for compliance at the corresponding point in time listed in Table A8-1 and ending when photometric stability is reached.
requirements.test_case: Measure intensities from the Table A8-1 time point until photometric stability; all values must be within min/max limits.

requirements.text: In case a lamp (function) uses more than one light generating technology, the corresponding intensity requirements of the lamp (function) shall be tested following the strictest time requirements according to paragraphs 2.1.1. to 2.1.3. for the combination of them and checked for compliance.
requirements.test_case: Apply the strictest time requirements of 2.1.1 to 2.1.3 and verify intensities comply with min/max limits.

requirements.text: In case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour), the corresponding minimum intensity requirements of a lamp (function) shall be tested and checked for compliance at all points in time starting at the corresponding point in time listed in Table A8-1 and ending when photometric stability is reached.
requirements.test_case: If run-up behaviour is doubtful, continuously measure intensity from the Table A8-1 time point to photometric stability; minimum values must be met throughout.

requirements.text: A separate approval is required for each retro-reflective device listed in paragraph 1 (the retro-reflector of Class IA or IB).
requirements.test_case: Check that the integrated retro-reflector has its own R150 approval, separate from the lamp functions' approvals.

requirements.text: The approval number assigned to the approved type of retro-reflector shall be marked on the device following the requirements of paragraph 3.3.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the device and verify that the assigned approval number is marked in line with paragraph 3.3.

requirements.text: Every retro-reflective device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the Unique Identifier as referred to in the 1958 Agreement and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2. or, the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2.
requirements.test_case: Inspect drawings and samples to verify a marking space large enough for the UI or the approval marking plus the paragraph 3.3.4.2 markings.

requirements.text: All markings on the retro-reflective device shall be clearly legible and indelible.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the markings and perform a rub/durability check; the markings must remain clearly legible.

requirements.text: With regard to the size of the approval marking, the value for "a" shall be as defined in Table 1 (minimum 5 mm for retro-reflectors of Class IA or IB).
requirements.test_case: Measure the approval mark and verify that dimension "a" is at least 5 mm.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for a circle enclosing "E" and the approving country number.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall consist of the four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the 4- to 6-digit sequential number of the approval.

requirements.text: The sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
requirements.test_case: Verify by inspection that the sequential number is adjacent to the E-circle.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall consist of the symbols identifying the retro-reflective device prescribed in paragraph 3.2.5 (IA or IB).
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the correct class symbol (IA or IB) as per Table 1.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall consist of the number of this Regulation followed by the letter "R" and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for "150R" followed by the two-digit series of amendments.

requirements.text: If the approval marking is replaced by the Unique Identifier, the Unique Identifier mark shall follow the format in the example shown in Figure I.
requirements.test_case: Compare the UI mark on the device against the Figure I format.

requirements.text: The retro-reflective devices shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the device for the applicant's trade name or mark.

requirements.text: In case of a retro-reflector of Class IA or IB, the retro-reflective device shall bear the word "TOP" inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: If rotation is restricted, verify that "TOP" is inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface.

requirements.text: The approval marking or the Unique Identifier and the markings in paragraph 3.3.4 shall be clearly legible on the retro-reflective device.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the device to confirm the approval marking/UI, trade name and TOP marking are clearly legible.

requirements.text: Where a single approval mark is affixed on grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, the marking shall be visible after their installation.
requirements.test_case: Install the lamp on a representative vehicle or fixture and verify that the single approval mark remains visible.

requirements.text: Where a single approval mark is affixed on grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of the lamps that transmits light can be removed without at the same time removing the approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or the Unique Identifier.
requirements.test_case: Review the construction to confirm that every light-transmitting part cannot be removed without removing the single approval mark.

requirements.text: The size of the components of a single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
requirements.test_case: Measure the single approval mark components and compare them against the smallest minimum size required by the applicable Regulations.

requirements.text: The requirements contained in sections 5. "General specifications" and 6. "Individual specifications" and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections of UN Regulation No. 48, and its series of amendments in force at the time of application for the retro-reflecting device type approval, shall apply to the retro-reflector where its verification at the moment of retro-reflecting device type approval is feasible.
requirements.test_case: Check the retro-reflector against the applicable UN R48 sections 5 and 6 provisions for M1 vehicles that can be verified at component approval; all must be met.

requirements.text: The retro-reflective devices shall be so constructed that they function satisfactorily and will continue to do so in normal use.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the retro-reflector and review the results of all Annex 6/7 tests; it must function satisfactorily throughout.

requirements.text: The retro-reflective devices shall not have any defect in design or manufacture that is detrimental to their efficient operation or to their maintenance in good condition.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the samples; there must be no design or manufacturing defect affecting operation or maintenance.

requirements.text: The components of retro-reflective devices or parts thereof shall not be capable of being easily dismantled.
requirements.test_case: Attempt to dismantle the retro-reflector by hand without tools; the components must not separate easily.

requirements.text: The outer surface of retro-reflective devices shall be easy to clean.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the outer lens surface over the retro-reflector; it must be easy to clean.

requirements.text: The outer surface of retro-reflective devices shall not be rough and any protuberances the outer surface of retro-reflective devices may exhibit shall not prevent easy cleaning.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the outer surface by sight and touch; it must not be rough and any protuberances must not prevent cleaning.

requirements.text: There shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflectors when in normal use.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the assembled lamp; the inner surface of the retro-reflector must not be accessible in normal use.

requirements.text: If the retro-reflector consists of a combined retro-reflecting optical unit and filter, the unit and filter must be so designed that they cannot be separated under normal conditions of use.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the construction; the optical unit and filter must not be separable under normal conditions of use.

requirements.text: The colouring of retro-reflecting optical units and filters by means of paint or varnish is not permitted.
requirements.test_case: Review the BOM and inspect the optical unit and filter; their colouring must not come from paint or varnish.

requirements.text: The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous intensity of the retro-reflective device shall be within the limits for the night-time colour of the light retro-reflected from that device, as defined in UN Regulation No. 48.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates; they must lie within the UN R48 red night-time colour limits.

requirements.text: For testing the colour of the retro-reflective device, the device shall be illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A, with an angle of divergence of 1/3° and an illumination angle of β1= β2= 0° or, if this produces a colourless surface reflection, an angle as specified in Annex 4, Part 1, paragraph 1.1. shall be used.
requirements.test_case: Perform the colour measurement with Illuminant A at 1/3° divergence and β1=β2=0°, or at the Annex 4 angle; confirm the test conditions are recorded.

requirements.text: When tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB shall meet the dimensions and shape requirements set forth in Annex 5.
requirements.test_case: Measure the shape and dimensions of the retro-reflector; they must comply with Annex 5 (e.g. non-triangular shape).

requirements.text: When tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements as specified in paragraphs 5.1.4. to 5.1.5.
requirements.test_case: Perform photometric and colorimetric measurements; the results must meet paragraphs 5.1.4 and 5.1.5.

requirements.text: When tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB shall meet the physical and mechanical requirements set forth in paragraph 5.1.7., depending on the nature of the materials and construction of the retro-reflective devices.
requirements.test_case: Carry out the physical and mechanical tests of paragraph 5.1.7; all must be passed.

requirements.text: After verification of the general specifications (paragraph 4.) and the specifications of shape and dimensions (Annex 5), the ten samples of the retro-reflector shall be subjected to the heat resistance test described in Part 1 of Annex 6 and, at least one hour after this test, examined as to their colorimetric characteristics in paragraph 5.1.5. and RI in paragraph 5.1.4., for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° or, if necessary, in the position defined in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.
requirements.test_case: Run the Annex 6 Part 1 heat test on the ten samples and measure colour and RI at 20' and 0°/0° at least one hour later; they must meet 5.1.4 and 5.1.5.

requirements.text: The two samples of the first group of retro-reflectors shall be subjected successively to the water penetration test (Part 2 of Annex 6) and then, if this test is satisfactory, to the tests for resistance to fuels and lubricants (Parts 1 and 2 of Annex 7).
requirements.test_case: Perform the water penetration test, then the fuel and lubricant resistance tests on group 1; the samples must pass.

requirements.text: The two samples of the second group of retro-reflectors shall, if necessary, be subjected to the corrosion test in Part 4 of Annex 6, and then to the abrasive-strength test of the rear face of the retro-reflective device in Part 5 of Annex 6.
requirements.test_case: Perform the corrosion test (if applicable) and the rear-face abrasion test on group 2; the samples must pass.

requirements.text: The two samples of the third group of retro-reflectors shall be subjected to the test for stability in time of the optical properties of retro-reflective device in Part 3 of Annex 4.
requirements.test_case: Perform the Annex 4 Part 3 stability-in-time test on group 3; the samples must pass.

requirements.text: The two samples of the fourth group of retro-reflectors shall be subjected to the resistance to weathering test (Part 6 of Annex 6).
requirements.test_case: Perform the Annex 6 Part 6 weathering test on group 4; the samples must pass.

requirements.text: After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group must have a colour which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.5.
requirements.test_case: Measure the colour of each group after testing; it must meet paragraph 5.1.5.

requirements.text: After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group must have a RI which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.4., verified only for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° or, if necessary, in all positions specified in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.
requirements.test_case: Measure RI at 20' divergence and 0°/0° for each group after testing; it must meet paragraph 5.1.4.

requirements.text: Where more than one axis of reference, or a range of axes of reference, is specified by the manufacturer, the photometric measurements of the retro-reflector shall be repeated, making reference each time to a different axis of reference or to the extreme axis of reference of the range specified by the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Repeat the photometry for each specified axis or the extreme axes of the range; each set must meet Table 3.

requirements.text: For photometric measurements of the Class IA or IB retro-reflector, only the illuminating surface defined by the planes contiguous to the outermost parts of the optical system, as indicated by the manufacturer and contained within a circle of 200 mm diameter, shall be considered, and the illuminating surface itself shall be limited to 100 cm2.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the measured illuminating surface lies within a 200 mm circle and does not exceed 100 cm2.

requirements.text: The manufacturer shall specify the perimeter of the area of the retro-reflector to be used for photometric measurements.
requirements.test_case: Check that the drawings define the perimeter of the photometric area.

requirements.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values for red retro-reflectors of Class IA and IB at an angle of divergence of 20' shall be equal to or greater than 3.00∙10^2 mcd∙lx-1 at β1 = 0°/β2 = 0°, 2.00∙10^2 mcd∙lx-1 at β1 = ±10°/β2 = 0°, and 1.00∙10^2 mcd∙lx-1 at β1 = ±5°/β2 = ±20°, as given in Table 3.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement at 20' divergence; RI must be ≥300 at 0°/0°, ≥200 at ±10°/0° and ≥100 at ±5°/±20° mcd/lx.

requirements.text: RI values of the retro-reflector lower than those shown in the last two columns of Table 3 are not permissible within the solid angle having the centre of reference as its apex and bounded by the planes intersecting along the lines (β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°) and (β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°).
requirements.test_case: Scan RI within the defined solid angle; no value may fall below the corresponding Table 3 minimum.

requirements.text: Where the Class IA or Class IB retro-reflector is intended to be installed with its H plane at a mounting height less than 750 mm above the ground, the RI values are verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
requirements.test_case: If the mounting height is <750 mm, verify the RI values down to 5° below horizontal only; they must meet Table 3.

requirements.text: The testing of the colour for the retro-reflector (night-time colour) shall be carried out according to the method described in paragraph 4.2.1.
requirements.test_case: Confirm the colour test report follows the 4.2.1 method.

requirements.text: The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous flux of the retro-reflector must be within the limits for the night-time colour red as specified in UN Regulation No. 48.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of the reflected light; they must lie within the UN R48 red night-time limits.

requirements.text: The retro-reflectors of Classes IA and IB shall be subjected to the tests in the chronological order given in Table 4 (Chronological order of tests, Classes IA, IB, IIIA and IIIB).
requirements.test_case: Review the test report and confirm the samples a to j were tested in the sequence and allocation of Table 4.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector of Classes IA and IB shall withstand the heat test according to Part 1 of Annex 6 (48 h at 65 °C ± 2 °C) without distortion on visual inspection.
requirements.test_case: Expose the samples for 48 h at 65 °C ± 2 °C and visually inspect; pass if no distortion is visible.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector of Classes IA and IB shall withstand the water test according to Part 3 of Annex 6 (10 min in normal position and 10 min in inverted position) followed by visual inspection, colorimetry and photometry limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.
requirements.test_case: Immerse the samples 10 min normal and 10 min inverted, inspect, then check colour and photometry; pass if no water ingress and the values are met.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector of Classes IA and IB shall withstand the motor fuels test according to Part 1 of Annex 7 (5 min) on visual inspection.
requirements.test_case: Expose the samples to motor fuel for 5 min and visually inspect; pass if no visible deterioration.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector of Classes IA and IB shall withstand the oils test according to Part 2 of Annex 7 (5 min) on visual inspection, followed by colorimetry and photometry limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.
requirements.test_case: Expose the samples to lubricating oil for 5 min, inspect, then check colour and photometry; pass if no deterioration and the values are met.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector of Classes IA and IB shall withstand the corrosion test according to Part 4 of Annex 6 (24 hours, 2 hours interval, 24 hours) on visual inspection.
requirements.test_case: Perform salt-spray exposure 24 h + 2 h interval + 24 h and visually inspect; pass if no corrosion that impairs performance.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector samples of Classes IA and IB shall meet the general specifications and the shapes and dimensions of Annex 5 by visual inspection, as listed in Table 4.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect all ten samples against paragraph 4 and Annex 5; pass if no non-conformity is found.

requirements.text: After the heat test, the retro-reflector of Classes IA and IB shall meet the colorimetry requirements of paragraph 4.2. (visual inspection, trichromatic coordinates in case of doubt) and the photometry requirements of Part 1 of Annex 4 limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°, with complete photometry on the designated samples.
requirements.test_case: Measure colour and the coefficient of luminous intensity at 20' and β1 = β2 = 0° (and complete photometry on two samples); pass if within the required limits.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector of Classes IA and IB shall meet the stability in time test according to Part 3 of Annex 4, followed by colorimetry according to paragraph 4.2. and photometry limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.
requirements.test_case: Perform the stability-in-time test, then check colour and photometry; pass if the values remain within the required limits.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector of Classes IA and IB shall meet the resistance to weathering test according to Part 6 of Annex 6, followed by colorimetry according to paragraph 4.2. and photometry limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.
requirements.test_case: Perform the weathering exposure, then check colour and photometry; pass if the values remain within the required limits.

requirements.text: With respect to photometric performance of mass-produced retro-reflective devices, no measured value of any retro-reflective device chosen at random shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Measure the photometric values (CIL) of a randomly chosen production retro-reflector and confirm that no value is more than 20 % below the prescribed minimum.

requirements.text: The chromaticity coordinates of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall be complied with.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of a randomly chosen production retro-reflector and confirm that they lie within the prescribed red colour boundaries.

requirements.text: One of the retro-reflectors of sample A, after the sampling procedure in paragraph 2., shall be tested for resistance to water penetration according to the procedure described in paragraph 1. of Part 2 of Annex 6 and shall pass the test; if the test on sample A is not complied with, both retro-reflective devices of sample B shall pass the same procedure.
requirements.test_case: Subject a production retro-reflector sample to the Annex 6 Part 2 paragraph 1 water penetration test and confirm that it passes, or that both sample B devices pass if the first fails.

requirements.text: When the RI of the retro-reflective device is measured for an angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, it shall be ascertained whether any mirror effect is produced by slightly turning the device; if there is any such effect, a reading shall be taken with an angle β of β1 = -5°, β2 = 0°.
requirements.test_case: Turn the device slightly at β1 = β2 = 0° on the goniometer; if a mirror effect occurs, verify that a reading at β1 = -5°, β2 = 0° is taken and recorded.

requirements.text: With an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, or the angle specified in paragraph 5. of this Regulation, and an angle of divergence of 20', retro-reflective devices which are not marked "TOP" shall be rotated about their axes of reference to the position of minimum RI, which must conform to the value specified in paragraph 5. of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Rotate the device about its reference axis at β = 0° and 20' divergence, find the minimum RI position, and verify the RI meets the paragraph 5 value.

requirements.text: When the RI of a retro-reflective device not marked "TOP" is measured for the other angles of illumination and divergence, the retro-reflective device shall be placed in the position corresponding to the value of ε of minimum RI; if the specified values are not attained, the device may be rotated about its axis of reference ±5° from that position.
requirements.test_case: Measure RI at all other specified angles with the device fixed at the minimum-RI ε position (±5° allowed) and verify all values meet the specified limits.

requirements.text: With an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, or the angle specified in paragraph 4. of this Regulation, and an angle of divergence of 20', retro-reflective devices marked "TOP" shall be rotated about their axes ±5° and the RI must not fall below the prescribed value in any position assumed by the device during this rotation.
requirements.test_case: Rotate the TOP-marked device ±5° about its reference axis at β = 0° and 20' divergence and verify RI never falls below the prescribed value.

requirements.text: If for the direction β1 = β2 = 0°, and for ε = 0° the RI of the retro-reflective device exceeds the specified value by 50 per cent or more, all measurements for all angles of illumination and divergence shall be made for ε = 0°.
requirements.test_case: Measure RI at β = 0°, ε = 0°; if it is ≥150 % of the specified value, verify all further measurements are made at ε = 0° and meet the limits.

requirements.text: For testing the retro-reflection the retro-reflective devices shall be illuminated with a CIE Standard Illuminant A (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) and measured as described in Part 1 of Annex 4.
requirements.test_case: Verify the test report shows illumination with CIE Standard Illuminant A and measurement per Annex 4 Part 1.

requirements.text: The measuring distance for photometry of the retro-reflective device shall be chosen such that at least the limits for the angles δ, γ and η are respected, but not lower than 10 m.
requirements.test_case: Check the test set-up records a measuring distance of at least 10 m with δ ≤ 10', γ ≤ 10' and η ≤ 80'.

requirements.text: For retro-reflective devices of Class IA or IB, the shape of the illuminating surfaces shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape, as prescribed for retro-reflectors mentioned in paragraph 2.1., from an observation distance of 10 metres.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the retro-reflector illuminating surface from 10 m and confirm it cannot be easily confused with the triangular shape of Class IIIA/IIIB retro-reflectors.

requirements.text: In the case of moulded plastics reflectors of retro-reflecting devices of Classes IA, IB, the retro-reflective device shall be kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at a temperature of 65 °C ± 2 °C after which the sample shall be allowed to cool for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.
requirements.test_case: Condition the retro-reflector 48 h at 65 °C ± 2 °C dry, cool 1 h at 23 °C ± 2 °C, and confirm test conditions were met before inspection.
